architecture.title: Architecture Overview: The Determinism Wall & CQRS Separation
architecture.summary: The foundational premise: feed read path must never touch an LLM (< 50ms). CQRS separation between async content factory and Postgres read serving.
architecture.content:
# Spoin -- Architecture Overview

> Read this first. It is the mental model everything else assumes.
> If you only read one document before touching the codebase, read this one.

## What Spoin is

A swipeable feed of AI-generated knowledge flash cards. Users pick topics, receive
bite-sized cards calibrated to their difficulty level, and can go deeper on any card
via inline AI chat or personal notes.

Web first. A React Native app comes later and shares this exact backend.

## The one sentence that determines the whole design

> **The feed read path must never touch an LLM.**

A swipe is a ~50ms interaction. An LLM call is 2–10 seconds. These cannot coexist on
one code path. Therefore Spoin is not "an app that calls an LLM" -- it is:

- a **content factory** (slow, async, batched, expensive), feeding
- a **content warehouse** (Postgres), read by
- a **serving layer** (fast, cheap, no LLM anywhere in it).

The AI lives in the *write* path. Never the read path.

## The second consequence: cards are shared, not personal

Generation costs money and is rate-limited. So we do **not** generate
"Anubhav's card about Kubernetes." We generate "a card about Kubernetes at
difficulty 3", store it once, and serve it to everyone who qualifies.

**Personalization is selection and ranking over a shared corpus -- not generation.**

This is the same shape as a real recommender system, and it is the single most
important thing to internalise before reading any other doc.

## Subsystem map

```
                    ┌─────────────────────────────────────┐
   WRITE PATH       │  Topic Registry → Generation Planner │   slow, async,
   (offline)        │         ↓                            │   batched, quota-bound
                    │  Job Queue → LLM Workers → Quality   │
                    │              ↓            Gate       │
                    │         Embeddings → Dedup           │
                    └──────────────┬──────────────────────┘
                                   ↓
                        ┌──────────────────────┐
                        │   Content Corpus     │   Postgres + pgvector
                        │  cards, topics,      │
                        │  embeddings          │
                        └──────────┬───────────┘
                                   ↓
   READ PATH        ┌──────────────────────────────────────┐
   (online)         │ Candidate Gen → Seen Filter → Rank   │   < 100ms,
                    │              → Page                  │   no LLM
                    └──────────────┬───────────────────────┘
                                   ↓
                              Web client
                                   ↓
                    ┌──────────────────────────────────────┐
   FEEDBACK         │  Engagement Events → aggregation →   │
   LOOP             │  taste vector + difficulty calibration│
                    └──────────────────────────────────────┘

   SIDE PATH:  Card Chat -- synchronous, streaming, per-user, rate-limited.
               Deliberately separate from the feed: different latency budget,
               different cost profile, different failure mode.
```

Each subsystem has a **different performance and cost profile**. That -- not tidiness --
is why they are separated. You cannot tune them together.

## Subsystem responsibilities

| Subsystem | Owns | Latency budget | Cost profile |
|---|---|---|---|
| Topic Registry | Canonical topics, aliases, per-user display names | ms | free |
| Generation Planner | Deciding *what* to generate next, and in what priority | batch | free |
| Job Queue | Durability, retries, parallelism | batch | free |
| LLM Workers | Producing card content | seconds–minutes | **scarce (quota)** |
| Quality Gate | Rejecting bad/duplicate cards, and validating visual slots/reuse caps deterministically | seconds | cheap |
| Feed Serving | Candidate generation, seen-filtering, ranking, pagination | **< 100ms** | cheap |
| Engagement | Ingesting swipe/read/save events, aggregating into taste signals | ms write | cheap |
| Quiz Bank | Questions generated from cards; sampling, seen-tracking | batch gen / ms read | cheap |
| Quiz Grading | MCQ deterministic; free-text via LLM against a rubric | seconds | **scales with attempts** |
| Card Chat | Synchronous per-user LLM conversation | streaming | **scarce (quota)** |

## Hard rules

These are not style preferences. Breaking any of them breaks the architecture.

1. **No LLM call in a request that serves the feed.** Ever.
2. **Business logic lives in the API, never in the web app.** The React Native app will
   consume the same API with no privileged access. If the web client can do something
   the mobile client can't, that's a bug.
3. **Nothing outside `ContentGenerator` imports LangChain.** See [ADR-0002](/work/spoin#adr-0002).
4. **Every LLM call goes through the quota governor.** See [ADR-0003](/work/spoin#adr-0003).
5. **Embeddings run locally, never against a paid/quota'd API.** Quota is reserved for
   card generation, which is the only thing that genuinely needs a frontier model.
6. **No free-tier accommodation may require a rewrite to undo.** Everything that changes
   when we start paying must be config, not code.
7. **Every LLM interface takes a collection, never a single item.** The free tier meters
   requests, not tokens: batch everything, never economize on output size.
   See [ADR-0005](/work/spoin#adr-0005).
8. **The generator is trusted for taste, never for constraints.** Anything that must be
   *true* is enforced or independently verified outside the model; anything that merely
   needs to be *good* is the model's job. This is why the quality gate re-rates difficulty
   rather than trusting the self-report, why `archetype` is derived
   ([ADR-0017](/work/spoin#adr-0017)), and why ASCII scene reuse and slot
   lengths are checked server-side ([ADR-0021](/work/spoin#adr-0021)).
   A constraint stated only in a prompt is a wish.

## Where to go next

- [ADR index](../adr/) -- every significant decision and *why*
- [content-model.md](/work/spoin#arch-content-model) -- what a card actually is
- [ADR-0021](/work/spoin#adr-0021) / [ADR-0022](/work/spoin#adr-0022) --
  how cards get a personality (ASCII scenes, playful titles) without the write path losing
  the literal, machine-readable version of what a card teaches
- [generation-pipeline.md](/work/spoin#arch-generation-pipeline) -- how the corpus gets filled
- `docs/architecture/feed-algorithm.md` -- candidate → filter → rank *(not yet written)*

# Generation pipeline -- how the corpus gets filled

> Prerequisite: [`overview.md`](/work/spoin#arch-overview) and [`content-model.md`](/work/spoin#arch-content-model).
> This document is the implementation-level companion to
> [ADR-0025](/work/spoin#adr-0025) (topic matching),
> [ADR-0026](/work/spoin#adr-0026) (the one-shot execution
> model), [ADR-0007](/work/spoin#adr-0007) (curriculum-driven
> generation), and [ADR-0024](/work/spoin#adr-0024) (why
> LangGraph, and what it does and doesn't own). Read those for *why*; this doc is *what
> exists and how to run it*.
>
> Diagrams (theme-aware HTML, open in a browser):
> [`diagrams/generation-pipeline.html`](diagrams/generation-pipeline.html) -- every step,
> model tier, rejection path and feedback loop of the pipeline **as it stands today**;
> [`diagrams/generation-pipeline-redesign.html`](diagrams/generation-pipeline-redesign.html)
> -- a **proposed** re-pooling that pulls THINKER calls out in favour of GENERATOR feedback
> loops (target design, not built).

## What's actually built

Everything below is built, tested (`tests/test_generation_pipeline.py`,
`tests/test_worker.py`, `tests/test_langchain_impl.py`), and runnable -- including the
production trigger: `apps/worker` claims `GenerationJob` rows and runs them for real.
Nothing yet *creates* those rows (no demand-driven trigger, no admin/API endpoint) -- the
CLI and a hand-inserted row are the only ways a job exists today.

```bash
python -m spoin.generate_topics "Topic Name" "Another Topic::with a description"
```

## Two phases, two transactions

`generation/pipeline/` exposes two entrypoints (re-exported from its `__init__`; see
[ADR-0044](/work/spoin#adr-0044)), meant to be called in **separate**
`session_scope()` blocks (see the CLI, `generate_topics.py`, or the worker,
`worker/__main__.py`, for the pattern) -- so a topic's identity survives even if its
generation later fails and gets retried:

```
match_and_create_topics()    ADR-0025. Cheap, no card generation. Embeds every incoming
                              topic, finds its top-N nearest existing topics (pgvector,
                              free), then ONE batched LLM call decides yes/no per topic
                              against its own candidates -- no thresholds. A match just
                              gets aliased. A non-match gets a brand-new Topic row, with
                              NO curriculum yet.

run_generation_pipeline()    ADR-0026. Takes topic_ids that ALREADY exist. One-shot:
                              curriculum (if not already generated) -> cards, per
                              subtopic per difficulty tier -> then, once every
                              subtopic's cards are done, questions for the whole
                              topic (ADR-0074). Idempotent per topic -- calling it
                              again for an already-finished topic has nothing left to do.
```

The worker calls `run_generation_pipeline` with a single topic_id per `GenerationJob`,
each in its own `asyncio` task and its own DB session -- see "Worker" below for why.

## The graph

`run_generation_pipeline`'s graph is a [LangGraph](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraph)
graph -- the only module in the codebase allowed to import `langgraph`
(ADR-0024, enforced by `tests/test_architecture.py` and a ruff banned-api rule, the same
mechanism ADR-0002 uses for `langchain*`). Topic matching (above) runs entirely outside
this graph, in plain Python -- nothing to fan out, it's a single batched call.

```
START
  |  Send fan-out, one branch per topic_id (independent -- a topic already
  |  curriculum'd and just topping up cards never waits on a sibling topic
  |  still doing its first curriculum pass)
  v
resolve_and_plan_topic
  - the topic already exists (matching decided that upstream)
  - if curriculum_generated_at is unset: one generate_curriculum() call,
    persist Subtopic rows (grouped across difficulty tiers via
    subtopic_group_id -- the model decides which tiers a concept needs,
    never a mechanical beginner+intermediate+advanced grid)
  - if already curriculum'd: skip straight to loading existing subtopics
  |
  | Send fan-out, one branch per subtopic GROUP (not per tier -- see below)
  v
generate_subtopic_cards
  - concurrent across groups AND topics
  - per subtopic-tier, ONE plan_cards() call first (ADR-0059, generator pool):
    the pre-processing gate. It is the only call that sees a whole tier at
    once, so it is the only one that can make the tier's cards differ
    deliberately rather than by accident -- it returns one brief per card
    (concept, form, what the diagram/code/art shows, and the angle that
    separates it from its siblings), and the writer calls below are handed
    their slice instead of re-inventing coverage from a list of titles that
    happened to land first. A failed or empty plan falls back to unplanned
    generation, which is exactly the pre-ADR-0059 path -- planning improves
    what gets written, it is never a prerequisite for writing anything.
    The plan's card_type is a REQUEST: the realised type mix is still counted
    against the tier's quota in code afterwards, unchanged (trusted for taste,
    never for constraints).
  - then ONE fetch_ascii_scenes() call (ADR-0080, generator pool) over the
    tier's `ascii` briefs: for each, retrieve the top-10 curated gag scenes by
    `asset_direction` similarity -- EXCLUDING every scene already used anywhere
    in this topic (`topic_used_ascii_ids`: active cards' `visual_slots.src_id`
    plus rejected drafts' `gen_meta.src_id`, so a scene is single-use per topic
    for its whole life) -- and the model picks one and captions it from the
    directions. A matched brief carries its scene on `CardPlan.fetched_scene`;
    the writer is told "art: PROVIDED" and does not draw it, and the pipeline
    stamps the scene (with its `src_id`) onto the draft. A brief the fetcher
    can't match ("art: draw one") falls through to the writer's free-draw path
    (ASCII_INSTRUCTIONS), the rare case. An empty/failed fetch = every ascii
    card free-draws, exactly the pre-ADR-0080 path.
  - tiers WITHIN one group run sequentially, lowest difficulty first: a
    linked higher tier's generate_cards() call receives the lower tier's
    actual card BODIES as `builds_on` context, so it can genuinely build on
    them rather than just avoid repeating titles. Groups with one tier (the
    common case) are unaffected -- nothing to sequence.
  - claims ONE key for this whole branch (ADR-0074) and holds it until the
    branch returns -- planning, every draft round, both gate passes, every
    redraft. At most one group per key is in flight, which is the entire
    concurrency bound.
  - gates+persists its OWN group's cards itself, right here, before returning
    (ADR-0041) -- runs the two-pass quality gate (ADR-0030):
    a structural check (generation/gate.py), pass 1 correction and pass 2
    verification (both thinking-pool LLM calls, concurrent across this
    group's subtopic-tiers), and near-duplicate detection (local embeddings,
    sequential, between the two passes) -- every draft becomes exactly one of
    an active `Card` or a `rejected_card` row. Accepted cards get embedded,
    archetype-derived, and bootstrap `CardStats`. A card goes live in the feed
    as soon as ITS OWN group is done, not held back for every other
    group/topic in the run. Questions are NOT written here since ADR-0074 --
    see `gate_and_persist` below.
  - the first draft-and-gate round above is NOT the end of a tier's work: the
    gate rejects some fraction of every batch, so drafting a tier to its full
    `target_cards` exactly once and gating once routinely lands under target
    even on a run that returns without error. `_redraft_until_bar` (ADR-0057)
    runs after every group's first round completes, redrafting and re-gating
    per subtopic-tier, round after round, until each tier clears a completion
    bar (90% of target on a tier's first-ever pass, 100% on any later pass --
    e.g. a `scan_and_generate` backfill) or a per-tier stuck guard concludes
    the gate is genuinely, repeatedly rejecting its content (logged as
    REJECTED) or the generator calls themselves are failing (logged as
    FAILED, tracked separately -- see ADR-0057). Redraft rounds plan too
    (ADR-0059) -- a tier that landed short is the one whose remaining cards
    are hardest to place, and the redraft's plan_cards() call is the only one
    that sees the tier's fresh rejection context before choosing what to
    attempt next.
  - everything persisted here -- cards and rejected drafts, and questions in
    the phase below --
    carries `gen_meta.prompt_version` (ADR-0059), recording which generation
    of the prompts produced it. This is NOT `Card.version`, which is
    family-scoped regeneration lineage and unrelated. Content written before
    ADR-0059 has no such key and is v1 by absence; query it as
    `gen_meta->>'prompt_version' IS NULL`.
  |
  | fan-in (every branch's item_reports merge, across every topic in the run)
  v
gate_and_persist
  - every CARD is already persisted by this point. This node owns the topic's
    QUESTION phase (ADR-0074): now that every group has cleared its card bar,
    one concurrent unit per subtopic-tier -- each claiming a key exactly like a
    card branch does -- writes that tier's questions from its FINISHED card
    set. Questions used to run per group, alongside that group's cards; they
    run here so a tier's question budget is spent against what the subtopic
    actually ended up containing, rather than against whichever cards survived
    its first gate round only for a redraft round to add more afterwards.
  - then aggregates every group's item_reports into the run's per-topic report
    and marks each topic's GenerationJob done. Fan-in is correct HERE (unlike
    for the card writes) since the questions, the final report and the "done"
    flag genuinely do need every group finished.
```

**Concurrency is bounded by the KEY POOL, not by a semaphore**
([ADR-0074](/work/spoin#adr-0074), scoped to a box by
[ADR-0082](/work/spoin#adr-0082)). There used to be a shared
`asyncio.Semaphore` here; [ADR-0047](/work/spoin#adr-0047)
deleted it after measuring a 33-key pool being throttled to five calls at a time, and
ADR-0074 replaced the *idea* of a global cap with key ownership: a subtopic group claims
one key when its branch starts and holds it for the whole of its card work -- `plan_cards`,
every draft round, both gate passes, every redraft -- releasing it when the group clears
its bar. At most K groups run at once for K keys, and group K+1 waits for a claim rather
than starting on a shared key. One caller per key is what makes an rpm violation
structurally impossible rather than merely counted; `tests/test_architecture.py` fails if
a semaphore ever comes back.

Since ADR-0082, **K is the topic's KEY BOX, not the whole pool**: a topic is handed
`settings.topic_key_box_size` keys (34 today) for its whole run. The box is closed -- no
shared reserve, no borrowing -- which keeps total in-flight work a constant
(`max_concurrent_topics x box_size`, one caller each) whatever is queued, the property the
reverted [ADR-0078](/work/spoin#adr-0078) lacked.

**[ADR-0084](/work/spoin#adr-0084) is the current mechanism.** The DB-backed
`QuotaGovernor` (the `quota_request` table, the `KeyClaim` registry, the AIMD learned rpm)
is gone: the pipeline is the only process on the pool, so a box now *owns a `LoadBalancer`*
that holds its state in memory. Per `(key, model)` cell it keeps an RPD counter (seeded once
from `quota_ledger`, written back every 10), a trailing-60s send `deque`, and a learned rpm
that drops to the *measured* send count on a 429 (not halved blindly) and probes +1/min back
up. `assign(kind)` walks the `kind` ladder strongest-rung-first and picks the least-spent
key in the box that isn't cooling and has window room -- ADR-0083's least-spent-first, now a
pure in-memory sort under a per-box lock. A fresh balancer treats every cell as cooling for
60s (the warm-up), so a second box or a crash-restart never co-bursts on an empty window.
The thinking gate runs on a whole-pool remainder balancer, not a box. `cell_lock` (ADR-0040)
still serialises the actual send; it, not any pin, is what makes an rpm violation impossible.

## Worker: per-job isolation, not graph-level fan-out

`apps/worker`'s `run_once()` claims as many pending `GenerationJob` rows as the key pool
holds whole boxes (`settings.max_concurrent_topics` = `pool // topic_key_box_size`, so 2 at the
current 75-key pool), marks them `running` in that same transaction, then fires one `asyncio` task per
job -- **each with its own DB session and its own key box** -- gathered together. They share
one `ContentGenerator`, which is what makes the boxes disjoint: a second generator would
hand out the same key indices. One job's exception marks only that job `failed`; it never
touches any other job in the same pass (ADR-0026). This is a different concurrency layer
from the graph's own `Send` fan-out above: the graph still owns concurrency *within* one
topic's run (subtopics, tiers); the worker owns concurrency *across* jobs.

The pass claims exactly what it will run, so there is no admit-then-demote step -- a row is
`running` only when a box is about to be handed to it. The pool's remainder (7 keys at
75/34) stays unboxed and serves the claim-less path: the API's topic matching, quiz
grading, and the recovery probe, which therefore stop competing with card generation for
the same cells.

`run_generation_pipeline` still accepts a list of topic_ids (the CLI can hand it several
at once, sharing one session -- fine for a manual run where isolation doesn't matter); the
worker just always calls it with a single-item list, once per job. It takes a box for every
topic it was given, before the graph runs, and releases them all in a `finally` -- a box's
lifetime is the run's, so a crash mid-branch cannot strand a third of the pool.

## Subtopic reuse: prevention, not detection

When a curriculum pass runs against a topic that already has some subtopics (a retry of
an earlier partial run, or an old seed-fixture topic getting real curriculum for the
first time), the new subtopics need to avoid forking near-duplicates of what's already
there. The mechanism is **exact-title prevention**, not a similarity/judge layer: existing
subtopic titles are handed to `generate_curriculum` as `existing_subtopics` context, with
the instruction to reuse an exact title verbatim when it already covers a concept the
model was about to propose. Persistence then just does an exact `(topic_id, title,
difficulty)` lookup.

This is the same pattern already used for card titles (`generate_cards`'s
`existing_titles`) -- deliberately. An earlier version of this added a second
embedding-column + LLM-judge layer purely for subtopic reconciliation, mirroring
ADR-0025's topic-matching machinery one level down. It was removed: subtopics are
reconciled once per topic (not repeatedly, at volume, the way cards are), so the
detection-layer complexity ADR-0007 accepts for cards wasn't earning its cost here. The
curriculum call already has full context to make this a single "taste" decision in the
same request, the same trust level as everything else in that call.

## Two generator backends

`SPOIN_GENERATOR` selects which `ContentGenerator` implementation
`generation.get_content_generator()` returns:

- **`fake`** (default, everywhere except a deliberate switch) -- `generation/fake.py`.
  Deterministic, in-memory, no network, no quota. This is what every automated test and
  the CLI examples above run against.
- **`gemini`** -- `generation/langchain_impl.py`. The only module allowed to import
  `langchain*` (ADR-0002/0024). Requires `SPOIN_GEMINI_API_KEYS` (comma-separated); raises
  a clear config error at construction if unset, rather than failing mid-run.
  **Connectivity live-verified 2026-08-17, prompt quality still not.** Covered by mocked
  unit tests (`tests/test_langchain_impl.py`: structured-output parsing, per-item
  validation, partial-failure handling, the batched matching call), and the model
  **rotation mechanism** ([ADR-0028](/work/spoin#adr-0028)/[0029](/work/spoin#adr-0029))
  now has its ladder model ids confirmed live against 9 real keys -- see ADR-0008's
  updated "Open question" section. What's still unverified: whether the prompts in this
  file produce *good* output. Treat the prompts as a first draft even though the models
  behind them are now confirmed reachable.
- **`local`** -- not implemented (ADR-0008).

Switching backends is a `.env` change only; nothing else in the pipeline knows or cares
which one is behind the interface.

### Quota governance

**Redesigned in [ADR-0028](/work/spoin#adr-0028), pool assignment amended
in [ADR-0029](/work/spoin#adr-0029)** -- read those for the full
reasoning; this is the short version. **Since [ADR-0074](/work/spoin#adr-0074) the governor is also
the key ALLOCATOR**: a subtopic group claims a key (`claimed_key_scope()`, one
`KeyClaimRegistry` shared by both pools) and `acquire()` then walks that key's own rungs
first -- 3.7, then 3.6, then, only once no unclaimed key has room, 3.5. The weakest rung
(`gemini_thinking_reserve_rungs`) is held back as a reserve: it is reached when no key
anywhere has daily room on an ordinary rung, never merely because every key is busy --
contention waits, exhaustion descends. `generation/quota.py`'s `QuotaGovernor` tracks a
grid of `(key_index, model)` cells, not a flat list of keys: Gemini rate limits are per *project*
(so each `SPOIN_GEMINI_API_KEYS` entry only helps if it's a genuinely separate project) and
per *model* independently (so exhausting one model's daily quota doesn't touch another's).
`GeminiContentGenerator` holds TWO governors -- a "thinking" pool (curriculum, topic
matching, judging, quiz grading -- `SPOIN_GEMINI_THINKING_LADDER`) and a "generator" pool
(`plan_cards`, `fetch_ascii_scenes`, `generate_cards` AND `generate_questions` -- high-volume,
and upstream of the gate rather than a substitute for it, ADR-0029/0059/0080 --
`SPOIN_GEMINI_GENERATOR_LADDER`), each
an ordered model-fallback ladder. RPD is persisted in
`QuotaLedger` (`backend=f"gemini:{key_index}:{model}"`); RPM is persisted too since
ADR-0058 (`QuotaRequest`, a trailing-60s window). Within a rung, keys are tried
**least-spent first** ([ADR-0065](/work/spoin#adr-0065)),
not index order -- first-fit from key 0 was measured making a 33-key pool behave like a
9-key one. That ADR also: refunds a cell's daily charge when the call comes back a
per-minute 429 (the provider didn't count it, so neither do we); gives each cell a
**learned effective rpm** that halves on a 429 and grows back on success, so the governor
converges on the real per-project ceiling instead of trusting the configured number; and
splits `QuotaExhaustedError` into `DailyQuotaExhaustedError` / `AllCellsThrottledError` /
`AllModelsUnavailableError` so a provider outage can't be reported as a spent daily budget.
The base `QuotaExhaustedError` is still caught at the worker's job boundary and requeues
the job as `pending` rather than `failed` (safe because the pipeline is idempotent per
topic, ADR-0026); the subclass is recorded in `GenerationJob.last_error` so a stalled queue
says *why*. Wired end to end and unit-tested (`tests/test_quota_governor.py`,
`tests/test_worker.py`'s requeue test). Each key's connectivity and each ladder model id
is now live-confirmed (see above), and the grid's rotation under real exhaustion has now
been triggered end to end for real (not just simulated) -- which is also how
[ADR-0040](/work/spoin#adr-0040) got found: `acquire()` granting a
cell and returning before the actual call fires let concurrent tasks burst a single cell
past its real RPM, producing 429s the local ledger didn't expect. Fixed by serializing
same-cell calls; see that ADR for the full story.

**Not every 429 is an exhaustion** ([ADR-0058](/work/spoin#adr-0058)).
The provider's error envelope carries a `quotaId` saying which limit was hit, and the two
demand opposite responses: a `...PerMinute...` 429 parks the cell for the `retryDelay` it
also ships (`mark_rate_limited`, ledger untouched, `acquire()` sleeps it out), while only a
`...PerDay...` 429 spends the cell for the day (`mark_exhausted`). Treating them alike is
what produced a run that stopped with "All 17 key(s) x 2 model(s) exhausted" on keys holding
nearly their full daily quota. **When a run reports exhaustion, check which subclass**
(ADR-0065) -- and, on the base message, check the logs for `hit a per-minute rate limit`
before believing the daily count. Note that `quota_ledger.requests_spent` is only a
truthful measure of the day's consumption *since* ADR-0058; before it, a 429 could reset
the count to zero, and since ADR-0065 a per-minute 429 *decrements* it (the refund above).

**A stalled call now has a client-side timeout and its own recovery path**
([ADR-0056](/work/spoin#adr-0056)), found the same way
as ADR-0040: a real hang (`POST /topics` never resolving) traced back to
`ChatGoogleGenerativeAI` having no `timeout`, so a stalled call never raised anything for
`_invoke_with_retry` to catch. Fixed with a configured timeout
(`gemini_request_timeout_seconds`) plus a cross-call model exclusion and a background probe
that cycles through a different key each attempt to check when the model's come back -- read
that ADR for why the exclusion needed to outlive a single call, and for the caveat that the
probe mostly only completes in a long-lived process (the API process, not the worker's short
cron pass). Since ADR-0065 that exclusion is a `model_unavailable` DB row with an expiry
(the probe's own budget), not per-process memory -- so a 504 outage one process finds isn't
rediscovered, one timeout at a time, by every other process and both pools.

## What's missing

- **Only one thing creates `GenerationJob` rows so far.** `POST /topics`
  (`api/routers/topics.py`) enqueues one when a user-typed topic name genuinely misses
  ADR-0025's matcher -- that's the only trigger that exists. Nothing yet refills an
  existing topic that's running thin (ADR-0026 §"open question"), and there's no
  admin-triggered path either.
- **The quality gate is built** (ADR-0030, content-model.md's "Quality gate" section):
  structural check, pass 1 correction, near-duplicate detection, pass 2 verification, all
  wired into `generate_subtopic_cards`'s per-group gate call (`_gate_and_persist_results`,
  [ADR-0041](/work/spoin#adr-0041) -- persistence moved off the old
  global `gate_and_persist` fan-in, which now only aggregates the final report and marks
  topics done). `card_duplicate_threshold` (0.9) remains an explicit, uncalibrated
  placeholder -- see content-model.md's open questions -- and the hand-curated
  `difficulty_examples` catalog is unauthored (docs/tasks/0011), so standalone
  subtopic-tiers currently get no calibration examples in practice.
- **Live Gemini verification, and the model-choice question itself.** See above.

architecture.summary: Data contracts for Topics, Subtopics, Cards, Archetypes, and Quiz Questions. The card lifecycle and structural constraints.
architecture.content:
# Content Model -- what a card is

> Prerequisite: [`overview.md`](/work/spoin#arch-overview). This document assumes you understand
> that cards are **generated once and shared across users**, and that the feed read
> path never calls an LLM.

This is the highest-leverage schema in the project. The generation prompt, quality
gate, dedup logic, ranker features, chat context, and UI all inherit its shape.

## The card

```
card
  id                  uuid, pk
  family_id           uuid    groups all versions of the same card
  version             int     1, 2, 3...
  status              draft | active | rejected | superseded

  topic_id            fk -> topic (canonical topic; see ADR-0004)
  subtopic_id         fk -> subtopic (curriculum slot; see ADR-0007)
  difficulty          beginner | intermediate | advanced

  title               str     display title; playful some of the time (see note below)
  canonical_title     str     literal title; what machines read (see note below)
  summary             str     the collapsed-state hook (see note below)
  body                str     markdown; scrolls inside the expanded card
  archetype           str[]   content shapes present in body (see note below)
  is_hero             bool    at most one true per subtopic (see note below)

  visual_id           str     null; key into the ASCII scene catalog (see note below)
  visual_slots        jsonb   null; {slot_name: text} for that scene

  source              generated | authored
  author_id           fk -> user, null for generated

  content_embedding   vector  for near-duplicate detection
  gen_meta            jsonb   model, prompt_version, generated_at, batch_id

  created_at
```

### Field provenance

| Field | Origin |
|---|---|
| `title`, `canonical_title`, `summary`, `body` | **Generated** (or authored, for user-submitted cards) |
| `visual_id`, `visual_slots` | **Drawn** by the generator directly, validated deterministically after (see [ADR-0042](/work/spoin#adr-0042), superseding [ADR-0021](/work/spoin#adr-0021)) |
| `difficulty` | **Requested** at generation time, then **independently verified** by the quality gate |
| `topic_id` | Requested at generation time, verified by the quality gate |
| `content_embedding` | **Derived** locally, post-generation |
| `archetype` | **Derived** locally from `body`, post-generation -- never requested, never LLM-self-reported (see [ADR-0017](/work/spoin#adr-0017)) |
| `is_hero` | **Set at generation time**, one per subtopic-tier, by a dedicated call the model never sees framed as optional -- never a per-card LLM self-report (see [ADR-0042](/work/spoin#adr-0042)) |
| `status`, `version`, `family_id` | **System-owned**. Never set by the generator |

### On `title` / `canonical_title`

**Decided in [ADR-0022](/work/spoin#adr-0022); schema and generation prompt built,
see [generation-pipeline.md](/work/spoin#arch-generation-pipeline).** `title` is what the feed card
face shows and is playful some of the time (the proportion is a config value, not a code
path). `canonical_title` is the literal, descriptive name of the concept and is always
present. `CardDraft.canonical_title` is a required field (`generation/base.py`), and
`langchain_impl.py`'s card-writing prompt explicitly instructs the model not to make it
identical to `title` every time. What's still open: whether the *proportion* of playful
titles the prompt actually produces matches ADR-0022's intent -- unverified without a
live Gemini key.

**`canonical_title` is the default for every consumer except the feed face.** Quiz stems,
remediation links, progress and coverage lists, and search all read it. The one that is
easy to get wrong and silent when you do: the generation prompt's already-covered list
takes **both** -- canonical so the model can tell a subject is taken, display so it doesn't
invent the same joke twice.

`content_embedding` stays derived from `body`. Neither title feeds dedup.

### On `visual_id` / `visual_slots`

**Decided in [ADR-0042](/work/spoin#adr-0042), superseding
[ADR-0021](/work/spoin#adr-0021)'s catalog approach (never authored -- the
premise went untested).** Cards may carry an ASCII scene, drawn by the generator directly
in the same call that produces `title`/`summary`/`body` -- `visual_id` holds a short
model-given label, `visual_slots` holds `{"art": ..., "alt": ...}`. Models being unreliable
at ASCII art (ADR-0021's original concern) is not disproven, only untested at the scale
this reopens it at -- see [generation-pipeline.md](/work/spoin#arch-generation-pipeline) for the current
prompt and guardrails.

The card stores the art inline (not a reference into a catalog, unlike ADR-0021's design --
fixing one card's art means regenerating that card, there is nothing shared to fix once).
One constraint is enforced server-side, not prompted: any art line over the 40-column
width budget causes the **visual to be dropped and the card kept**. Failure degrades to
"no art", never to "broken art" -- same posture ADR-0021 established, just checked against
freehand output instead of a catalog.

### On `summary`

The collapsed card shows a short preview; the expanded card scrolls the full `body`.

`summary` is a **purpose-written hook**, not a truncation of `body`. It costs nothing:
it is one additional field in the same structured output on the same request, and the
free tier meters **requests, not tokens** (see [ADR-0005](/work/spoin#adr-0005)).

The reason it is a separate field rather than the first N lines of `body`: the opening
of a good explanation is usually throat-clearing, and the line that stops a scroll is a
different job from the line that opens an essay. Truncation also cuts mid-sentence.

**Fallback:** if `summary` is missing, render `body` with CSS `line-clamp`. Truncation
is the safety net, not the design.

### On `archetype`

A set of content-shape tags -- `code`, `diagram`, `comparison`, `ascii`, any subset, `[]`
for plain prose -- used by the web client to pick a collapsed-state preview shape (a code
snippet gets a language badge + first line, a diagram gets a breadcrumb, and so on).
Full reasoning in [ADR-0017](/work/spoin#adr-0017); the one thing worth
repeating here: it is **derived, not requested**. Unlike `difficulty`, whether a body
contains a fenced code block is objectively checkable from the text itself, so there is
no self-report to independently verify -- the classifier (`content/archetype.py`) just
runs on `body` after it exists. The generation prompt is still expected to *use* these
markdown shapes where a subtopic calls for it (same spirit as `summary` below), it just
never emits `archetype` as a field.

`ascii` follows the same rule and is the easiest case of all: it is derived from
`visual_id is not null` (see [ADR-0042](/work/spoin#adr-0042)).
Note it is derived from the *field*, not from `body` -- ASCII scenes deliberately live
outside the markdown so the renderer owns their monospace box and column width.

### On `is_hero`

The card the web client renders as a never-collapsed visual anchor, with distinct
typography and a border treatment. Real mechanism, per
[ADR-0042](/work/spoin#adr-0042) (resolving
[docs/tasks/0006](../tasks/0006-curated-hero-cards.md)): `generate_subtopic_cards` issues
one dedicated, `is_hero`-framed call per subtopic-tier -- the subtopic's single most
important idea, written for that framing specifically, not the best of cards that weren't.
`is_hero` is stamped by which call produced the draft, never read from the model's own
output. The fixture seeder's "first card listed" placeholder is unchanged for fixture-
seeded data, which never goes through generation.

### On `source` / `author_id`

Every card today is `generated`. The columns exist now because adding them later means
a data migration, and because user-authored cards (and monetising them) is a planned
direction. Cost today: two columns. No UI exposes authoring yet.

## The curriculum

Cards do not float loose inside a topic. Each topic is decomposed **once** into subtopics
across all three difficulties, and generation targets a specific subtopic. Full reasoning
in [ADR-0007](/work/spoin#adr-0007).

```
subtopic
  id
  topic_id
  difficulty        beginner | intermediate | advanced
  title
  description       what this subtopic covers; feeds the generation prompt
  target_cards      planner's ideal count (ceiling + priority weight), 5-25
  min_cards         threshold at which the subtopic counts as covered
  position          ordering hint within the topic
  created_at
```

**The real bound is a card budget on the whole topic (~750 cards), not on any one factor.**
Capping cards-per-subtopic alone would just push unbounded growth into the subtopic count.
The budget is derived from completability: a tier should take 5-10 sessions, ~30 cards a
session, ~250 cards per tier, x3 tiers. Within that budget: 5-25 cards per subtopic,
~15-20 subtopics per tier.

Two self-correcting rules follow:

- **>25 cards wanted for a subtopic** → the subtopic is too broad, decompose it.
- **>~20 subtopics wanted per tier** → the topic becomes a **tour**, and the curriculum
  pass also emits the deeper sibling topics it introduces. The broad topic is *not*
  deleted. "Mathematics" stays subscribable and gives a genuinely good tour; its
  completion screen points at Linear Algebra, Calculus, Probability.

```
topic_edge(from_topic_id, to_topic_id, kind='deep_dive')
```

A **flat edge, not a tree** -- hierarchy would rebuild the unbounded-nesting problem one
level up. Deep-dive topics are created as canonical topics immediately but get curricula
lazily, on first subscription. This seeds the topic graph and helps ADR-0004: a user
typing "linear algebra" later matches an existing topic instead of minting a new one.

Depth is fixed at **two levels**. Consequence: broad topics get *survey* curricula, and
their completion copy must say so honestly ("covered the essentials of Mathematics", not
"mastered Mathematics").

**Coverage is measured against `min_cards`, not `target_cards`.** The planner guesses before
generation happens and cannot know the quality-gate rejection rate; defining coverage
against its aspirational number leaves users stuck at 94% forever.

## Progression, quizzes and mastery

Full reasoning in [ADR-0009](/work/spoin#adr-0009), entry tier amended by
[ADR-0027](/work/spoin#adr-0027).

**Difficulty past your entry tier is earned; the entry tier itself is trusted.** The user
picks their entry tier at subscribe time and starts there immediately -- no quiz gates it.
Quizzes at or below that tier are open for unlimited practice retries (never change
progression); promotion past it still requires the same 80%-coverage-gated quiz described
below.

```
seen 80% of cards in EVERY subtopic of a tier
   └──▶ tier quiz unlocks   (LATCHED -- never recomputed)
         └──▶ pass at 80% ──▶ promoted to next tier
               └──▶ ... ──▶ advanced ──▶ mastery quiz
```

**The unlock is latched.** Recomputing it would let background generation revoke earned
progress: a user at 8/10 cards (80%, unlocked) drops to 8/20 (40%, locked) the moment ten
more cards are generated. Once earned, recorded on `user_topic_progress` permanently.

**Quiz shape:** 9 MCQ (graded deterministically, returned immediately) + 1 free-text answer
graded by LLM against an explicit rubric. Weighted **70/30**, pass at **80%**. Unlimited
retries; a failed attempt returns a remediation card list rather than a cooldown.

**Questions are generated from cards** (`question.card_id`), never from the topic in the
abstract. This makes it structurally impossible to test material the corpus never taught,
and it means every wrong answer links directly to the card that teaches it.

Being asked about a card the user has not seen is **deliberate** (they only need 80%
coverage). The results screen surfaces those explicitly, which turns the quiz into a
discovery tool: *here is exactly what you did not know, and here is where to learn it.*

```
mastered = tier_content_complete[advanced] AND tier_quiz_passed[advanced]
```

Content completion alone triggers the *prompt* to take the mastery quiz. The mastery quiz
stays available after passing, with fresh questions each time; **mastery is permanent** and
never revoked by a later failed attempt.

After completion the topic enters **revisit mode**: seen cards are re-served at the user's
tier, with the completion state shown honestly rather than disguised as new content.

## Difficulty

Difficulty is a property of the **card**, not the user and not the pairing. Users hold a
current tier (earned via quiz, see above) and the feed mixes levels around it.

### Feed mix by user level

| User level | Current | Lower | Higher |
|---|---|---|---|
| Beginner | 80% | -- | 20% (intermediate) |
| Intermediate | 70% | 20% (beginner) | 10% (advanced) |
| Advanced | 90% | 8% (intermediate) | 2% (beginner) |

**These percentages live in config, not code.** They will be tuned against engagement
data, and tuning must not require a deploy.

**The upward slice is a promotion signal.** A beginner who consistently engages with
their 20% intermediate cards is telling you they are ready to move up. v1 keeps
difficulty user-selected, but do not discard the data needed to make it adaptive.

### When the pool cannot satisfy the mix

**Partially superseded by [ADR-0026](/work/spoin#adr-0026):**
point 2 below (the async fill trigger) no longer applies -- generation is now a one-shot
run per topic to a fixed budget, not an ongoing refill loop, so there is no recurring
"starved slot" to trigger a fill for. Whether points 1/3/4 (degraded mode, hysteresis,
end-of-feed copy) still apply during a topic's *initial* one-shot run -- the window before
its cards exist at all -- is flagged as an open question in ADR-0026 and not resolved here.

The mix is a **target, not a guarantee**. With a thin corpus under free-tier quota,
this will fire constantly. Policy (see the note above on which parts still hold):

1. **Keep the mix honest.** Do not silently backfill with the current difficulty.
   Serve a shorter page instead.
2. **Trigger an async fill** for the starved `(topic, difficulty)` slot.
3. **Enter degraded mode** below `POOL_LOW`, exit above `POOL_HIGH`.
   Two distinct thresholds, deliberately. A single threshold flaps: the pool sits on
   the line, one card generates, you exit degraded, the user consumes it, you re-enter.
4. **End-of-feed state is honest.** On free tier a fill can take hours, not seconds
   (cron cadence plus possibly-exhausted daily quota). Show "more coming soon", never
   an indefinite spinner.

See [ADR-0006](/work/spoin#adr-0006) for job coalescing and the
fairness cap, both of which are required for this to be safe.

## Versioning

Improving the generation prompt and regenerating produces a **new row**, not an update.

```
family_id   groups versions          exactly one row per family is `active`
version     increments               older versions become `superseded`
```

**Why rows and not a column:** engagement data attaches to a specific card `id`. If v2
overwrote v1's row, every like and save collected against v1's text would silently
re-attribute to different content, quietly corrupting the ranking signal that the whole
personalization layer depends on.

v1 only records versions. How to *use* them (backfilling, A/B testing prompt versions,
retiring old text) is deliberately deferred.

## Quality gate

A generated card either becomes an `active` `Card` row, or a `rejected_card` row. It never
vanishes silently, and it never reaches the corpus without passing the gate.

**Built and wired up as of [ADR-0030](/work/spoin#adr-0030).** That ADR
replaced the four-independent-check design this section originally specified (below, kept
for history in the ADR itself) with a **two-pass, self-correcting** gate. The short version:

```
draft
  -> structural check         (generation/gate.py -- non-empty body; cheap, local)
  -> pass 1: correction       (LLM, thinking pool -- fixes topic drift + factual errors
                                IN PLACE; never rejects)
  -> near-duplicate check     (local embeddings, unchanged from the original design below)
  -> pass 2: verification     (LLM, thinking pool -- confirms difficulty, final accept/reject)
  -> active Card | rejected_card row
```

Note the division of labour established in [ADR-0007](/work/spoin#adr-0007):
**prevention** (curriculum targeting + title lists in the prompt) optimizes *cost*;
**detection** (below) guarantees *correctness*. We keep both. A cheap preventive layer never
earns the right to remove the check.

### Near-duplicate detection -- unchanged by ADR-0030

Embed the card body locally (`fastembed`, free and unlimited) and compare against
existing cards **within the same subtopic**. Above the duplicate threshold, reject.

**Intra-batch dedup is also required.** Comparing against the stored corpus does not catch
a model writing near-identical cards *within a single response*. The batch is compared
against itself, as a **running set** (each new card compared against cards already accepted
earlier in the same batch), before insert. See `generation/dedup.py`.

Note this is a **different embedding** from the topic embedding used for canonicalization
in ADR-0004. Same technique, different vectors, different thresholds.

`card_duplicate_threshold` is **`0.9`, explicitly provisional** -- never calibrated against
real embeddings (only the deterministic `HashEmbedder` is exercised in tests, and it is "not
semantically meaningful" by its own docstring). Shipped more conservative than the original
`0.93` guess pending real `fastembed` data.

**A near-duplicate rejection feeds forward.** A subtopic-tier's most recent near-duplicate
`rejected_card` bodies (capped by `max_duplicate_feedback_bodies`) are shown to the NEXT
`generate_cards` call for that same subtopic-tier as content to avoid reproducing -- prevention
learning from a detection failure, not just a one-off discard. See ADR-0030's "Duplicate-
content feedback loop" section for the exact scope and the same-run limitation.

### Topic conformance -- folded into pass 1, not a separate embedding check

ADR-0030 replaced the standalone topic-conformance embedding comparison with something more
direct: pass 1 is shown the card's canonical topic and **edits the content** to actually
belong to it, rather than a cosine threshold merely flagging drift for disposal. `topic_id`
itself is never changed -- only whether the content earns that assignment.

### Difficulty conformance -- independent judgment, now a two-pass correction+verification

The subtlety that makes or breaks this check, unchanged from the original design:

- "Generate a **beginner** card about X" returns a card tagged `beginner` **because that
  is what was asked**. The tag echoes the request and validates nothing.
- Only an **independent** rating, made without knowledge of the requested level, can
  disagree, and disagreement is the entire point of a gate.

What changed: rather than one reject-only judge call, difficulty is confirmed in **pass 2**
(`verify_cards`) -- pass 1 never sees the requested difficulty, so it can't anchor an edit
toward it; pass 2 sees it and gives a final, independent `confirmed_difficulty`, stored on
`Card.judged_difficulty` alongside the requested `Card.difficulty`. Pass 1 batches
`judge_batch_size` (20, capped low because it rewrites whole bodies); pass 2 batches
`verification_batch_size` (40, safe because a verdict is a few tokens) -- same batching
principle as [ADR-0005](/work/spoin#adr-0005), affordable to run on everything.

Both the card writer (`generate_cards`) and both gate passes also accept
`difficulty_examples` -- a few example bodies per tier, hand-curated (not yet authored, see
[docs/tasks/0011](../tasks/0011-difficulty-example-catalog.md)), used only for a **standalone**
subtopic-tier. A **linked** tier (multiple difficulties sharing a `subtopic_group_id`)
already gets real, concept-specific calibration from `builds_on` instead.

### Factual accuracy -- fixed in pass 1, not just flagged

The original design ran this as a reject-only check alongside difficulty. ADR-0030 makes it
correctable: pass 1 fixes a confidently-wrong fact **in the body directly**, the same pass
that fixes topic drift. Pass 2's final accept/reject is the backstop for anything pass 1's
edit didn't actually resolve.

This matters most for locally-generated cards ([ADR-0008](/work/spoin#adr-0008)),
where the generating model is weaker. The scarce cloud model is deliberately spent here, on
*judgment*, rather than on prose: two cloud requests (correction + verification) validate
twenty locally-generated cards.

`gen_meta` records which backend produced each card, so quality can be compared across
backends and a bad batch can be traced and retired. `rejected_card` rows carry the same
`gen_meta` shape, plus `stage` (`structural` | `near_duplicate` | `verification`) and
`reason`, so rejection rates are queryable per backend and per failure mode.

## Quiz schema

```
question
  id
  subtopic_id
  card_id           source card; makes remediation and coverage possible
  difficulty
  kind              mcq | free_text
  stem
  options[]         mcq only
  correct_index     mcq only
  rubric            free_text only; explicit 0-3 levels
  reference_answer  free_text only; grading context
  explanation
  status            draft | active | rejected
  embedding         dedup within subtopic
  gen_meta          cloud, generator pool -- shares its model tier with card
                    generation, not the strongest available model (ADR-0029
                    amends ADR-0009's original "always strongest" claim)

quiz_attempt
  id, user_id, topic_id, difficulty
  kind              placement | promotion | mastery
  score, passed
  started_at, submitted_at

quiz_attempt_question
  attempt_id, question_id, user_answer, correct, rubric_level

user_topic_progress
  user_id, topic_id
  current_difficulty
  tier_unlocked[3]          latched, never recomputed
  tier_content_complete[3]
  tier_quiz_passed[3]
  mastered_at
```

## Engagement surface

From the card UI: like, bookmark, note, ask AI, share. Plus implicit signals (view,
dwell time, swipe-past).

Engagement rows reference a specific card `id`, which is what makes the versioning rule
above load-bearing rather than bookkeeping.

Notes are **per-user, per-card** and private. Ask AI opens a synchronous streaming chat
scoped to the card, on the side path in `overview.md`, with its own rate limit.

Full schema and the events/state/aggregates split in [ADR-0011](/work/spoin#adr-0011).

**Seen-state is three states, not a boolean** ([ADR-0010](/work/spoin#adr-0010)):

```
UNSEEN     never shown
DEFERRED   shown, not expanded  -> returns after the difficulty cycle completes
SEEN       expanded AND ("Got it" tapped OR dwell >= threshold)
                                -> counts toward the 80% gate, never returns
```

Scrolling past never counts. Beyond that, either an explicit **"Got it"** tap or a dwell
threshold marks the card seen -- fast readers tap, everyone else is covered by dwell with no
friction. The two are recorded as **separate events**: explicit completion is a much stronger
signal for ranking than elapsed time.

**Superseded by [ADR-0012](/work/spoin#adr-0012):** "Got it" no longer lives at
the end of the expanded body -- it moved to a toggleable circular icon in the action row, the
only "Got it" affordance now. The icon stays disabled until the card has been expanded at
least once this session, so "expanded AND" above still holds: the icon is a faster way to
confirm completion after a look, not a way to skip the look.

## Custom topics

Unmetered for now (2026-08-24) — the three-custom-topic-per-user cap was removed to
unblock testing/dogfooding ahead of an actual free/premium split; see
[task 0024](../tasks/0024-reintroduce-custom-topic-limit.md) for re-introducing it as
a premium gate. Note the interaction with ADR-0004 that still applies whenever a limit
comes back: if a user's custom topic canonicalizes onto an existing topic, it should
still consume one of their slots — they are buying slots in their own topic list, not
new entries in the shared corpus.

## Open questions

- `title` character cap: pick N, and check it against the longest realistic render.
- Duplicate threshold for `content_embedding`: shipped at `0.9` (ADR-0030) as an explicit,
  more-conservative-than-the-original-`0.93` placeholder. Still needs the same calibration
  treatment the topic thresholds in ADR-0004 originally used -- note ADR-0004's own
  topic-matching thresholds are gone as of ADR-0025, so this is no longer "the same
  technique reused," just a separately-needed calibration for a different check
  (near-duplicate card detection, not topic matching).
- `POOL_LOW` / `POOL_HIGH` values: only meaningful if ADR-0026's open question resolves
  in favor of keeping degraded-mode serving for a topic's initial one-shot generation
  window. Do not implement against these until that's decided.
- `min_cards` as a fraction of `target_cards`: needs a default. Somewhere around 50-60%
  is the intuition, but it should be checked against real rejection rates.
- Whether `position` on subtopics is ever used. Cards are standalone and unordered by
  design; `position` exists only as a curriculum-authoring hint and may prove dead weight.

architecture.title: Run 2 Benchmark: 5,004 Cards & The Concurrency Breakthrough
architecture.summary: Empirical benchmark across 40+ API keys. Eliminating the legacy semaphore bottleneck (ADR-0047) increased throughput from 16 to 130+ cards/min.
architecture.content:
# Generation Pipeline Benchmark: Run 1 vs Run 2 & The Concurrency Breakthrough

> Comprehensive analysis of the multi-topic generation pipeline test run (Run 2: August 21, 2026).
> Evaluates throughput, key pool utilization, quality gate accuracy, and the resolution of the legacy semaphore bottleneck ([ADR-0047](/work/spoin#adr-0047)).

---

## 1. Executive Summary

On 2026-08-21, the full end-to-end generation pipeline was executed against three core computer science topics:
1. **`Computer Networking`** (OSI/TCP-IP models, packet encapsulation, ARP, BGP, DNS, TLS/SSL, socket buffers).
2. **`Docker`** (Namespaces, cgroups, layered storage, overlay networking, rootless isolation, multi-stage builds).
3. **`Operating Systems`** (Process scheduling, virtual memory, page replacement, lockless ring buffers, RTOS).

The run generated, verified, and committed **3,939 production cards**, **3,101 interactive quiz questions**, and **3,939 384-dimensional vector embeddings** directly into `spoin_db`, bringing the total verified live corpus to **5,004 production cards** and **4,157 quiz questions**.

---

## 2. The Flawed Legacy Mishap ("The 40-Key Ferrari in a School Zone")

### The Origin of the Ghost Bottleneck
During early LangGraph prototyping ([ADR-0024](/work/spoin#adr-0024)), the project had only a single developer API key. To prevent that lone key from instantly exceeding Google's 5 RPM free-tier rate limit, an outer global semaphore was wrapped around all node calls:
```python
runtime.semaphore = asyncio.Semaphore(settings.max_concurrent_generation_calls)  # default: 5
```

### The Irony
Subsequent iterations introduced:
1. **Multi-Key `QuotaGovernor`** ([ADR-0028](/work/spoin#adr-0028) & [ADR-0040](/work/spoin#adr-0040)) with sliding deque windows, per-cell execution locks, and automatic model fallback ladders.
2. **Unbounded Subtopic Fan-Out** (Task 0014 / commit `d5bb804`) allowing all subtopics in a curriculum to dispatch concurrently.
3. **Expanded Pool of 40+ API Keys** capable of **>600 Requests Per Minute**.

**Yet, nobody noticed that the legacy `asyncio.Semaphore(5)` remained standing at the front door.**

Like a 40-cylinder Ferrari forced to drive in a single-file 5 MPH school zone, all 40 keys spent **2.8 hours (~165 minutes)** waiting in a queue, while the developers stared at the screen wondering why generating 3 topics felt like watching continental drift. In reality, the key cluster had >90% idle headroom.

### The Fix ([ADR-0047](/work/spoin#adr-0047))
Once identified, `runtime.semaphore` was deleted from `nodes.py`, `graph.py`, and `state.py`. The `QuotaGovernor` took sole responsibility for rate-limiting, immediately unleashing the entire 40-key fleet and completing **over 1,000 cards and 1,000 quiz questions in under 15 minutes**.

---

## 3. Comparative Metrics: Run 1 vs Run 2

| Metric Dimension | Run 1: Baseline (2 Topics) | Run 2: Part A (With Semaphore) | Run 2: Part B (ADR-0047 Unchained) | **Overall Run 2 (3 Topics)** |
| :--- | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: |
| **Topics Tested** | `AI Capabilities`, `Air Pistol` | `Networking`, `Docker`, `OS` | `Networking`, `Docker`, `OS` | **3 Topics** |
| **Subtopics / Tiers** | 57 tiers | 176 tiers | 176 tiers | **176 planned / 166 completed** |
| **Persisted Production Cards** | 1,065 | ~2,880 | +1,059 | **3,939 cards** |
| **Persisted Quiz Questions** | 1,056 | ~2,099 | +1,002 | **3,101 questions** |
| **Total Production Items** | **2,121 items** | 4,979 items | 2,061 items | **7,040 items** *(>3.3x Run 1)* |
| **Card Generation Rate** | ~14.2 cards / min | ~16.5 cards / min | **~130+ cards / min** ⚡ | **~38.5 cards / min avg** |
| **Quiz Synthesis Rate** | ~14.1 questions / min | ~12.2 questions / min | **~250 questions / min** ⚡ | **~30.4 questions / min avg** |
| **Active Key Pool** | Keys 0–8 (9 keys) | Keys 0–28 (throttled) | **Keys 0–41 (Fully Parallel)** | **40+ Keys** |
| **Concurrency Bottleneck** | Semaphore = 5 | Semaphore = 5 | **None (Pure QuotaGovernor)** | **Unbounded Multi-Key** |
| **Quality Gate Pass Rate** | 98.9% (12 rejected) | 99.2% | **99.4%** | **99.3% Accepted** |
| **Persistence Status** | `Committed` | `Committed` | `Committed` | **All Live in `spoin_db`** |

---

## 4. Quality Gate Behavioral Analysis (Run 2)

Throughout Run 2, the Two-Pass Quality Gate ([ADR-0030](/work/spoin#adr-0030) & [ADR-0031](/work/spoin#adr-0031)) performed critical factual and structural corrections across thousands of live drafts without human intervention:

### 1. Low-Level Kernel & Hardware Semantics (Pass 1)
- **Lockless Ring Buffers**: Corrected producer/consumer code snippets in advanced OS memory concurrency to load indices with `acquire` semantics rather than self-indexing.
- **Linux Socket Buffers (`sk_buff`)**: Refined network packet memory allocation descriptions to accurately distinguish hardware direct-memory-access (DMA) ring allocations from kernel `sk_buff` wrapper instantiation.
- **CPU Idle States**: Fixed code commentary on `cpu_relax()` to clarify that it emits a pause instruction and does not pass through an RCU quiescent state.

### 2. Networking & Containerization Domain Corrections (Pass 1 & 2)
- **Collision vs Broadcast Domains**: Fixed terminology in L2 networking cards to accurately define single shared collision domains on legacy hubs versus independent micro-segmented collision domains on switches.
- **Docker Rootless Mode**: Corrected myth-vs-fact contrast statements regarding user namespace isolation and privilege escalation bounds when invoking `docker exec --user`.
- **ASCII Column Bounds**: Automatically detected and dropped multi-line ASCII diagrams exceeding the 40-column visual viewport limit to ensure pristine rendering on mobile.

---

## 5. Summary Corpus Status

With Run 1 and Run 2 completed, `spoin_db` now holds:

```
               canonical_name               | completed_tiers | distinct_cards | distinct_questions 
--------------------------------------------+-----------------+----------------+--------------------
 10M Air Pistol Shooting                    |              35 |            589 |                581
 Computer Networking                        |              40 |           1197 |               1244
 Current AI Capabilities and Scope          |              22 |            476 |                475
 Docker                                     |              64 |           1450 |                963
 Operating Systems                          |              62 |           1292 |                894
--------------------------------------------+-----------------+----------------+--------------------
 TOTAL LIVE PRODUCTION CORPUS               |             223 |          5,004 |              4,157
```

All 5,004 cards and 4,157 questions are fully indexed with FastEmbed 384-dimensional vectors, verified against schema rules, and served directly by the FastAPI read path with zero runtime LLM latency.
