| `ordinal` | NOT NULL. Position within the document; makes a chunk citable as "part 3 of". |
| `text` | NOT NULL. |
| `embedding` | `Vector(1024)` — the same space as `card.content_embedding`, which is the point (ADR-0087, moved to 1024 by ADR-0092 here and ADR-0097 there). |
| `topic_tags` | `ARRAY(Text)`, GIN-indexed. |

#### Why `kind` is a real enum

> **Amended by [ADR-0096](/work/spoin#adr-0096).** "Retrieval treats
> the two kinds differently" is now literal in a stronger sense than this section
> imagined: `spoin_canon` is **not retrieved at all**. It is pinned into the system
> prompt per call type, and every retrieval filters to `topic_source`. The enum is
> more load-bearing for it, not less -- it is what makes the exclusion expressible.

Retrieval treats the two kinds differently and will keep doing so:
**Spoin canon** — how the product itself works, how a hook lands, the ASCII box rule,
[dual titles](/work/spoin#adr-0022), [archetypes](/work/spoin#adr-0017) — is
relevant to nearly every generation call regardless of subject. **Topic
source-of-truth** is relevant by subject. A free-text column would let a front-matter
typo create a silent third kind that nothing ever retrieves. Adding a third kind later
being a migration is correct: it is a real decision.

#### Why topic tags are slugs, not foreign keys

`the_spoin_universe` is a separate database, so a chunk **cannot** hold a foreign key
to `spoin_db_2`'s `topic` table. Tagging crosses that boundary by value.

Tags are produced by the same `normalize_topic_text` that `spoin` applies before
embedding a topic string: one normalizer, so tags and canonical topic names cannot drift
into two vocabularies. **That requirement is what moved the function.** ADR-0087 kept it
in `spoin`; the ingester that produces these tags lives in frog, which cannot import
`spoin`, so [ADR-0093](/work/spoin#adr-0093) moved it into
`frog.embeddings` and had `spoin` import it from there. They sit on `chunk` rather than `document` so a broad document can have
differently-tagged sections. GIN-indexed because they are a filter, even though the
filter is not applied by default.

#### Why idempotency is a content hash

The corpus will be re-delivered many times as it is supervised and revised.
Re-ingestion reads a file, hashes it, and skips the document if `content_hash`
matches; if it differs, that document's chunks are replaced in one transaction.

The alternative — a version field in front matter — is human-maintained, will be
forgotten at least once, and its failure mode is stale chunks silently surviving a
revision. A hash cannot be forgotten.

### Retrieval is cross-topic by default

A PostgreSQL card may legitimately ground itself in distributed-systems material.
`topic_tags` filtering is **available and not applied by default**.

The risk is real: retrieval can drag a card off its subtopic. The mitigation already
exists in the gate's topic-conformance check. But
[task 0038](../tasks/0038-frog-rag-and-hybrid-generation.md) is explicit that this
must be **inspected in Phase 3 by looking at actual retrieval scores on cross-topic
hits**, not assumed away.

## Consequences

**Easier.** Corpus revisions never touch production data. The universe database can be
dropped and rebuilt from the delivered corpus at any time — it is derived, not
authoritative — which makes ingestion experiments cheap in a way nothing else in this
project is. A card can cite what grounded it, which is the "we can back with grounding
why our material is high quality" claim made storable.

**Harder.** Two databases means two connection URLs, two alembic chains, and two
backup concerns. `the_spoin_universe` is rebuildable from the delivered corpus, so the
hourly Neon backup does not need to cover it — but that is now a fact someone has to
remember rather than infer. No cross-database joins: anything wanting topic metadata
alongside a chunk does two queries and joins in Python. Topic tags can drift from
canonical topic names if `normalize_topic_text` changes, the same coupling task 0001
already flags.

**Committed to.** Same Postgres instance, therefore same volume, therefore three
databases behind one prohibition.

## Alternatives considered

**Corpus tables inside `spoin_db_2`.** No new database, no second alembic environment,
joins work. Rejected: every corpus revision becomes a migration against production, and
the corpus is re-delivered *many times*. It also puts derived, rebuildable data in the
one database that must never be rebuilt.

**A second alembic environment inside `apps/api/`.** Keeps migrations under one roof.
Rejected on the wrong-database argument above — the safety of the chosen option is that
the universe environment structurally cannot read `SPOIN_DATABASE_URL`.

**frog manages its own schema with `create_all` or plain SQL.** Simplest today.
Rejected: no migration history for a store that will evolve as the corpus is revised,
and no way to reason about what shape a given ingestion run wrote.

**Topic tags on `document` only.** Fewer rows to keep consistent. Rejected: loses the
ability to tag one section of a broad document differently, which is exactly what a
dense authoritative source looks like.

**An explicit version field for idempotency.** Rejected on the forgotten-bump argument.

## Revisit when

- Phase 3's retrieval-score inspection shows cross-topic hits pulling cards off
  subtopic more often than the gate catches. The fix is a default `topic_tags` filter,
  and it amends this ADR.
- A third content kind appears. That is a migration, and worth a moment's thought about
  whether `kind` is still the right axis.
- The corpus grows past what a single-instance pgvector index serves at generation
  latency. That is a scaling decision, not this one.

adrs.title: ADR-0089: Generation is grounded in retrieved corpus context, and each card records the chunks that grounded it
adrs.summary: Both the drafter and the verifier read the same retrieved passages, and the grounding chunk IDs are stored on the card.
adrs.content:
# ADR-0089: Generation is grounded in retrieved corpus context, packed against a token budget, and each card records the chunks that grounded it

- **Status:** Accepted, **partially superseded 2026-09-05**
- **Date:** 2026-09-04
- **Deciders:** project owner, implementing session
- **Amended by the owner, 2026-09-05:** the token budget is gone and grounding is a
  **fixed top 2** — the alternative this ADR rejected below. Grounding itself, and the
  `grounded_chunk_ids` provenance, are unchanged and still stand. Two things the ADR
  did not know moved the answer; both are recorded in the rejected alternative and in
  `Settings.grounding_chunks`. The title's "packed against a token budget" no longer
  describes the code.

## Context

Today the writer drafts from parametric knowledge and the gate checks it *after the
fact* ([ADR-0030](/work/spoin#adr-0030)). There is no source-of-truth corpus
and no retrieval over one — verified: nothing in `generation/` or `content/` does
topic-level factual grounding. The truth guarantee for a product whose claim is
"quiz-gated mastery of true things" is entirely post-hoc.

That was tolerable while the drafter was `gemini-3.x-flash`. It stops being tolerable
under [ADR-0090](/work/spoin#adr-0090), which moves drafting onto
`ministral-3b/8b`. A 3B model's parametric recall is not a foundation.

[ADR-0087](/work/spoin#adr-0087) built the retrieval package and
[ADR-0088](/work/spoin#adr-0088) built the corpus store. This ADR says what
generation actually does with them.

## Decision

**Retrieval grounds generation upstream of the gate, context is packed against an
explicit token budget, and the chunk IDs that grounded a card are recorded on it.**

### Both drafters and thinkers retrieve

The verification pass grounds its factual check in **the same corpus the drafter
used**. This is the point of the design, not a nicety: a gate checking a grounded
draft against its own parametric memory reintroduces exactly the unreliability the
corpus exists to remove, and turns a disagreement between two models into a
coin-flip rather than a check against a source.

### Context assembly is capped, and the cap is a design budget

> **Superseded 2026-09-05.** The cap is `Settings.grounding_chunks = 2`, and there is
> no token budget. The throughput table below is still the right way to reason about
> prompt size, and its numbers are still the numbers — what changed is that two
> passages are bounded at roughly 1200 prompt tokens by the ingestion contract, so a
> budget had nothing left to decide. Read this section for the reasoning, not for what
> the code does.

`pack_by_tokens` ([ADR-0085](/work/spoin#adr-0085),
`generation/load_balancer.py`) already packs items against a prompt-token budget with
spillover. Retrieval context assembly reuses that posture rather than inventing a
second budgeting mechanism.

The budget matters more than it looks, because sustainable throughput is
`min(TPM / prompt_tokens, RPM)` and the target is ~34 calls/min for 600 cards/hr:

| prompt size | `ministral-3b` (1.3M TPM, 750 RPM) | `ministral-8b` (625k, 188) | `ministral-14b` (937.5k, 30 RPM) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 12k (today) | 108 | 52 | 30 |
| 20k | 65 | 31 | 30 |
| 30k | 43 | 21 | 30 |
| 40k | 33 | 16 | 23 |

`ministral-8b` drops below 34/min above ~18k tokens. `ministral-3b` holds to ~38k.
`ministral-14b` is RPM-capped at 30 and **can never reach 34 at any prompt size**.

**This is a budget to aim at, not a prediction.** Task 0038's build order is
deliberate on this point and this ADR does not pre-empt it: build frog, then
*measure* what prompts actually grew to from run logs, and only then sweep Mistral
concurrency at the real sizes. Picking a budget up front and hoping is the mistake
the gemini-saga was four weeks of.

### Provenance is recorded on the card

Retrieval returns chunk IDs alongside text, and the IDs are stored against the card
they grounded. "We can back with grounding why our material is high quality" is a
claim about **citability**, and a claim that cannot be checked is a slogan. Storing
the IDs is what makes a card auditable after the fact — including auditable for the
failure mode below.

### ⚠️ The corpus is the ceiling on card quality

A thin or wrong corpus produces confidently-grounded wrong cards, which are **worse
than parametric guessing** because they look sourced and because the gate is now
checking against the same bad source. This is the main risk the design takes on, it
is not mitigated by anything in this ADR, and it is why the corpus-authoring track is
supervised. Recorded here so the tradeoff is not rediscovered later as a surprise.

## Consequences

**Easier.** The truth guarantee moves upstream of the gate instead of resting on it.
A card can cite what grounded it. Cheaper, smaller, faster drafting models become
viable without quality collapse — which is the entire premise of ADR-0090.

**Harder.** Every generation call's prompt grows, and prompt size is now a throughput
input, not a detail — the table above is the whole reason the model choice is not
free. Two systems (drafter and gate) now share a dependency on corpus quality, so a
bad chunk fails silently in both directions at once. Retrieval adds a per-call latency
that did not exist, on a path already fighting for calls/minute.

**Committed to.** Prompt-size measurement before model selection, in that order.
Chunk-ID provenance on cards, which means a card outlives the chunks it cites and
something has to decide what a dangling citation means.

## Alternatives considered

**Ground the drafter only, leave the gate parametric.** Cheaper — the gate's prompts
stay small, and gate calls are on the scarcer thinking ladder. Rejected on the
coin-flip argument: a parametric gate judging a grounded draft is not a check, and
under ADR-0090 the two models are from different providers with different training,
so their disagreements would carry no information about truth.

**Keep post-hoc gating only, skip retrieval.** Zero new machinery. Rejected: it is
the status quo, and the status quo's reliability was underwritten by a model we are
leaving.

**A fixed top-k with no token budget.** Simpler. Rejected: chunk sizes vary, so a
fixed k has an unbounded token cost, and the table above shows token cost is exactly
what decides whether the target throughput is reachable at all.

> **Adopted 2026-09-05**, on the owner's decision, because the premise turned out to
> be false. Chunk sizes do *not* vary without bound: the ingestion contract rejects a
> section over `MAX_SECTION_CHARS` (2200), which is a hard check at ingest, not a
> guideline. At k=2 that caps grounding at roughly 1200 prompt tokens no matter what
> the corpus does — so the token cost of a fixed k is bounded after all, and a budget
> over it could never bind. A limit that cannot bind is the dead setting `8a8e64c`
> removed once already; keeping one here would have recreated it.
>
> The related `min_score` floor was also dropped, for a reason outside this ADR: the
> owner's commitment is that the curated corpus covers a topic before that topic
> exists in production, so there is no uncovered topic for a stray passage to be the
> best answer to. That is what a floor would have guarded against (ADR-0088's
> cross-topic risk), and it is guaranteed upstream instead.

**Record provenance as free text in the card body.** No schema change. Rejected: not
queryable, so it cannot answer "which cards did this retracted chunk ground?" — which
is the question provenance exists to answer.

## Revisit when

- Phase 4's measurement lands. If real prompt sizes push past ~38k, `ministral-3b`
  stops clearing the target rate and the model choice reopens — as does whether 2 is
  still the right depth. (The budget that would have cut depth is gone; depth is now
  the only lever, which makes this signal more directly actionable, not less.)
- A chunk is found to be wrong after cards have been generated from it. That is the
  first real test of whether stored chunk IDs are enough to act on, and the answer
  probably amends this ADR.
- Retrieval latency becomes a measurable fraction of a generation call.

adrs.title: ADR-0090: A hybrid generator routes drafting calls to Mistral and keeps thinking calls on Gemini
adrs.summary: The first step off the free-tier Gemini ladder, later completed by ADR-0103.
adrs.content:
# ADR-0090: One `HybridContentGenerator` routes generator-ladder calls to Mistral over raw `httpx` and keeps thinking-ladder calls on Gemini

- **Status:** Accepted, then **partly superseded** by
  [ADR-0103](/work/spoin#adr-0103) (2026-09-07)
- **Date:** 2026-09-04
- **Deciders:** project owner, implementing session

> ⚠️ **The routing table below is no longer what runs.** ADR-0103 moved the thinking
> ladder to Mistral too (`ministral-14b-2512`) and deleted `mistral_max_in_flight`.
> Only a prompt carrying a non-text part still goes to Gemini. What remains live in
> this ADR is its *reasoning* — the measurements, why a hybrid was right at the time,
> and the no-cross-provider-fallback rule, which is unchanged. Read ADR-0103 before
> trusting any routing claim here.

## Context

The [gemini-saga](../gemini-saga/README.md) ended at an undocumented, IP-keyed
**concurrency** ceiling: requests from this source IP simultaneously awaiting a
response shed with a hard wall between 3 and 4, shared across every key in the pool.
Adding keys bought nothing. Four weeks went into discovering a limit that was invisible
to quota accounting.

The [mistral-saga](../mistral-saga/README.md) measured Mistral before building on it —
the one rule that saga cost bought. Results:

- **No concurrency wall through N=5. Zero 429s in 641 calls.** Throughput rises with
  concurrency. The opposite of Gemini's behaviour.
- **Structured output is reliable at 12k tokens** — 646 calls, isolated `bad_schema`
  only, over OpenAI-compatible `POST /v1/chat/completions` with
  `response_format: {type: json_schema, strict: true}`.
- **This account can only call `ministral-3b/8b/14b` and `codestral`.** Everything
  Small/Medium/Magistral returns 429 with `x-ratelimit-limit-req-minute: 0` — a
  permanent zero allocation, not a transient throttle. `mistral-large` and
  `labs-leanstral` are 403 tier-gated. **There is no reasoning-capable Mistral model
  on this tier at all.**

That last point is what forces a hybrid rather than a migration. Mistral has the
throughput Gemini lacks; Gemini has the reasoning Mistral cannot offer here.

## Decision

**`HybridContentGenerator` implements the existing `ContentGenerator` ABC. The split
is by what a call PRODUCES: a call that produces a verdict runs on Gemini's thinking
cells; a call that produces prose runs on Mistral.**

### The routing table

Task 0038's draft table said to "confirm each method's real ladder against the code
before trusting this table." Confirmed against `langchain_impl.py`'s
`_invoke_with_retry` call sites — which turned up two methods the draft omitted
entirely, and one whose placement is a real decision rather than a lookup.

| Method | Produces | Routes to |
|---|---|---|
| `plan_cards` | a plan | **Mistral** |
| `fetch_ascii_scenes` (and the ASCII redraw call) | a scene + caption | **Mistral** |
| `generate_cards` | prose | **Mistral** |
| `correct_cards` | rewritten prose | **Mistral** |
| `generate_questions` | prose | **Mistral** |
| `repair_card_structure` | repaired prose | **Mistral** |
| `stream_topic_answer` | prose | **Gemini** (flash-lite) — see below |
| `generate_curriculum` | structure + judgment | **Gemini** |
| `match_topics` | a verdict | **Gemini** |
| `validate_topic_names` | a verdict | **Gemini** |
| `verify_cards` | **a verdict** | **Gemini** |
| `grade_free_text` | a verdict | **Gemini** |
| `claimed_key_scope`, `lease_key_box`, `release_key_box` | — | **Gemini** (box leasing is Gemini-pool-specific) |

Two methods the draft omitted: **`stream_topic_answer`** (AskAI,
[ADR-0077](/work/spoin#adr-0077)) and **`match_topics`**.

**AskAI stays on Gemini's flash-lite generator ladder** rather than moving to Mistral
with the rest of the prose calls (owner's decision, 2026-09-05). It produces prose, so
the rule above would put it on Mistral — but it is the one *user-facing, latency-visible*
call in the table, and it is low-volume compared to card generation. Keeping it on
Gemini reserves Mistral's throughput entirely for the batch work that needs it. This is
a capacity-allocation exception to the verdict/prose rule, not a revision of it; it will
still be grounded in frog like everything else.

#### `correct_cards` moves to the generator side, and `verify_cards` never does

This is the load-bearing line, and it is a **change to the ladder the code uses
today**: `correct_cards` currently runs on the thinking ladder as one half of
[ADR-0030](/work/spoin#adr-0030)'s two-pass gate. It moves to the generator
ladder, on both providers.

The two halves of that gate do genuinely different work, and treating the pass as one
unit had been hiding it:

- **`verify_cards` decides.** It returns accept/reject. That is a *constraint*, and
  CLAUDE.md's rule is that constraints are never trusted to the cheap path. It stays
  on the thinking cells permanently — not "for now", not "until Mistral improves".
- **`correct_cards` rewrites.** It takes a card and a criticism and produces better
  prose. That is *taste*, and taste is what the generator ladder is for.

What makes the move safe rather than a corner cut is
[ADR-0089](/work/spoin#adr-0089): correction happens **against a
retrieved source**, so the rewriting model is not being asked to recall a fact — it is
being asked to restate one it has been handed. Recall is the capability a 3B model
lacks and a frontier model was quietly compensating for; restatement is not. And the
verdict that follows is still Gemini's, so a bad correction is caught rather than
shipped.

This applies from the first pass, not only after a redraft round. If the corpus turns
out thin, this is the first decision to revisit — see "Revisit when".

**Applied to the Gemini path on 2026-09-05**, ahead of frog being wired in — the
owner's call, made knowing the retrieval premise is not yet live. Until the corpus
exists, `correct_cards` is running ungrounded on the lite ladder, which is the weaker
of the two conditions the decision was argued from. The revisit condition below is the
thing that catches it if that turns out to be a bad trade.

#### Why route by what a call produces

The routing rule and the ladder split ([ADR-0028](/work/spoin#adr-0028),
[ADR-0029](/work/spoin#adr-0029)) stay the same object, so there is
one list rather than two that drift. Both now say the same thing in the same words:
**verdict on the thinker, prose on the generator** — CLAUDE.md's "trusted for taste,
never for constraints", applied per call rather than per pass.

### Raw `httpx`, not `langchain-mistralai`

The probe already proved the exact request shape works at 12k tokens across 646 calls.
Raw `httpx` avoids a new LangChain dependency and a new
[ADR-0002](/work/spoin#adr-0002) `banned-api` entry. Responses parse into the
existing `_LenientWireModel` Pydantic models, so the wire/domain split is unchanged.

### Most of the Gemini machinery is not ported

**No key pool, no box leasing, no quota ledger, no load balancer for the Mistral side.**
Mistral needs one key, a send path, structured-output parsing, a modest in-flight cap,
and retry on 429/503.

ADR-0082/0083/0084/0086 — fixed key boxes, least-spent balancing, the per-box load
balancer, dispatch stagger and jitter — are all machinery built to survive a
concurrency ceiling that **Mistral was measured not to have**. Porting them would be
carrying four weeks of scar tissue onto a provider without the wound. If Mistral later
turns out to shed under load, the soak test is what finds it and this decision reopens.

### Failure counts stay three-way

Per CLAUDE.md and the pipeline's existing `_process_gate_item` fix: `bad_schema`,
gate rejection, and call failure are **three separate counts**. A call that never
returned a verdict is not the same fact as content that was judged and found bad. A
new provider is exactly the condition under which conflating them would misread a
transport problem as a quality catastrophe.

## Consequences

**Easier.** Drafting throughput stops being governed by an IP concurrency wall.
Generator-ladder volume comes off Gemini's budget entirely, which makes the thinking
ladder's much smaller daily budget go further. Provider risk is split: an outage at
either provider degrades half the pipeline rather than all of it.

**Harder.** Two providers means two failure vocabularies, two retry policies, and two
sets of rate-limit semantics to keep straight in logs. A drafting model that is much
weaker at instruction-following makes every instruction-only rule more fragile —
[task 0038](../tasks/0038-frog-rag-and-hybrid-generation.md)'s ASCII box rule is the
known live example, and it is deliberately left open for its own decision rather than
settled here. Raw `httpx` means we own the retry, timeout and parse code that LangChain
would have supplied.

**Committed to.** Gemini remains a hard dependency for judgment calls. This is not a
migration away from Gemini and should not be described as one.

## Alternatives considered

**Move everything to Mistral.** Simplest operationally, one provider. Impossible on
this tier: every reasoning-capable model returns a permanent zero rate limit or a 403.
The gate would run on `ministral-3b`, judging drafts written by `ministral-3b`.

**Stay entirely on Gemini.** No new provider, no hybrid complexity. Rejected: the
concurrency ceiling is the binding constraint on throughput and no amount of key-pool
engineering moved it — that conclusion is what the whole gemini-saga documents.

**`langchain-mistralai`.** Consistent with how Gemini is called, retries supplied.
Rejected: a new LangChain dependency and a new ADR-0002 boundary entry, to wrap a
request shape a committed probe has already exercised 646 times.

**Port the load balancer to Mistral.** Defensible on "it already exists". Rejected:
it solves a measured-absent problem, and the cost of carrying it is that a future
reader cannot tell which parts of it are load-bearing.

**Route by hand-written method list instead of by ladder.** Rejected: the ladder split
already carries the reasoning, and a second list would drift from it.

## Revisit when

- The soak test (30 minutes at the chosen concurrency) shows a slow-accruing penalty.
  Gemini's ceiling was invisible to short runs; if Mistral has one, this is what finds
  it, and the "no load balancer" decision reopens immediately.
- Phase 6's accept-rate comparison lands below the fixed thresholds: within ~10 points
  of the Gemini baseline passes; 10–25 points below is marginal and points at
  `ministral-14b` or restricting Mistral to the ASCII-fetch sub-task; more than 25
  points below fails and this ADR is superseded.
- **Corrected cards start failing verification more often than uncorrected ones.**
  That is the signal that moving `correct_cards` to the generator side outran the
  corpus, and the response is to move it back rather than to argue with the numbers.
  Phase 6 measures it for free — it already counts gate rejections separately from
  call failures.
- Someone proposes moving `verify_cards` to the generator side. It does not move.
  That is the one row in the table that is a rule rather than a placement.
- The account's tier changes and a reasoning-capable Mistral model becomes callable.
  The hybrid exists *because* one does not.

adrs.title: ADR-0092: `Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B` at 1024 dimensions, with a GPU/CPU device split
adrs.summary: A real embedder with an asymmetric query/passage interface, replacing the 384-dimension stand-in.
adrs.content:
# ADR-0092: `Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B` at 1024 dimensions, with an asymmetric query/passage interface and a GPU/CPU device split

- **Status:** Accepted
- **Date:** 2026-09-05
- **Amends:** [ADR-0087](/work/spoin#adr-0087) — replaces its "vectors stay
  384-dim, same model" commitment
- **Depends on:** [task 0039](../tasks/0039-embedder-never-reached-the-containers.md) —
  the reason a re-embed is happening at all
- **Completed by:** [ADR-0097](/work/spoin#adr-0097) — the
  "regeneration wipe" this ADR waits for below happened on 2026-09-05. `spoin_db_2` is
  1024-dim, the two databases no longer diverge, and there is one embedder rather than
  two.

## Context

Task 0039 established that `SPOIN_EMBEDDER` never reached the containers, so every
vector in `spoin_db_2` is `HashEmbedder` output rather than a semantic embedding. The
repair requires re-embedding everything.

**That is what makes this decision cheap.** Re-embedding is the expensive part of any
embedding-model change, and we are paying it regardless. Switching models now costs
approximately nothing; switching later costs a second full backfill. The window is
open exactly once.

Three constraints shape the choice.

**1. The generation pipeline moves to the owner's machine.** Only the app-serving
backend deploys online; generation runs manually on a home PC with an RTX 5070 (12GB).
There is no cron refill and no intention to automate one soon. So bulk embedding has a
GPU available and is not latency-sensitive.

**2. Something still embeds on the live request path.** Topic requests move to a queued,
manual flow — beta users are told generation takes up to two days — which removes most
of it. But AskAI's off-topic gate ([ADR-0077](/work/spoin#adr-0077))
embeds the user's question **every turn** and compares it against `topic.embedding`.
That cannot be queued.

**3. Dimension parity is not space parity.** Two different models that both emit 1024
floats produce vectors that are not comparable. A gate comparing a query vector from one
model against a topic vector from another is comparing noise, and nothing would raise.

## Decision

**The embedder is `Qwen/Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B`, 1024 dimensions, run on GPU for bulk work
and on CPU for the request path — the same weights on both devices.**

Verified before committing to it: the model exists and is widely used (~7M downloads),
and `onnx-community/Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B-ONNX` publishes fp16/int8/bnb4 exports, so the
CPU path is real rather than assumed.

0.6B is the deliberate size. A 4B model would score better and fits the 5070, but it
would be **GPU-only in practice** — and constraint 2 means something must run on a CPU
in the deployed backend. Choosing a model that cannot is choosing to break the gate or
to split the vector space. 0.6B is the largest size that keeps one model everywhere.

### The `Embedder` interface becomes asymmetric

Retrieval models are trained asymmetrically: a query and a passage are encoded
differently. Qwen3-Embedding expects queries wrapped as
`Instruct: <task>\nQuery: <text>` and passages left bare. Our previous model,
`bge-small-en-v1.5`, wanted its own query prefix — and **we were not applying it
anywhere**, which was a silent recall loss for as long as a real embedder was in use.

So `Embedder` grows `embed_query` and `embed_passage` rather than one `embed`. The
asymmetry is a property of the model, not of the caller, and an interface that hides it
makes forgetting it the default. `HashEmbedder` treats both identically, which is
correct — it has no notion of either.

### 1024 dimensions, and why the cost is irrelevant

5,491 cards × 1024 dims × 4 bytes ≈ 22MB. At this corpus size dimension is free, so
there is no reason to economise against quality. This supersedes ADR-0087's "vectors
stay 384-dim" — that commitment was made to keep corpus and card vectors comparable,
and comparability is preserved by both moving together, not by the number staying still.

### The two databases diverge temporarily, on purpose

`the_spoin_universe` moves to 1024 now. **`spoin_db_2` stays at 384 until the
regeneration wipe** — which happened on 2026-09-05 (ADR-0097); this section is history,
not current state. `spoin.domain.models.topic` reads `embedding_dim` at import time to
declare `Vector(...)`, so changing it before the columns change would make the ORM
disagree with the live schema and break every insert.

This is safe only because of a specific fact: nothing currently compares a card vector
to a chunk vector, and `spoin_db_2`'s vectors are hash output — meaningless in any
space. The divergence ends when the regeneration runs. It is a sequencing artefact with
a defined end, not a design.

### The CPU/ONNX path is deferred, not dropped

Bulk embedding on GPU is needed now; the CPU path is needed when the backend deploys,
which has not happened. Deferred to its own task rather than built speculatively — but
the interface is designed for it now, so adding it is an implementation, not a redesign.

**One thing to measure when it is built:** int8 ONNX quantization drifts from fp16 torch.
Typically cosine ≈ 0.99+, usually fine for a threshold gate — but "usually fine" is how
task 0039 happened. Measure the drift against the gate's actual threshold before
trusting it, and prefer the fp16 export if the drift is material.

## Consequences

**Easier.** Retrieval quality rises substantially from a genuinely weak baseline —
`bge-small-en-v1.5` was the weakest retrieval model on fastembed's list, and we were not
even applying its query prefix. The asymmetric interface makes that class of silent loss
structurally hard to repeat. GPU bulk embedding makes a full re-embed a minutes-long
operation, which makes future model changes cheap to evaluate rather than dreaded.

**Harder.** A new dependency (`sentence-transformers` + torch) that `fastembed` did not
need, and a device split to keep straight. Two vector spaces exist until the
regeneration — a real hazard, mitigated only by the fact that nothing compares them and
by this ADR saying so out loud. Every call site must now choose `embed_query` or
`embed_passage`, and choosing wrong is silent.

**Committed to.** One model on two devices. The moment a model is picked that cannot run
on a CPU, the AskAI gate needs a different design.

## Alternatives considered

**Stay on `bge-small-en-v1.5`, just fix the flag.** Smallest change. Rejected: it is the
weakest retrieval model available to us, and the re-embed that makes a switch free is
happening either way. Refusing the upgrade now means paying a second backfill later to
get it.

**`snowflake-arctic-embed-l` via fastembed.** No new dependency, ONNX-ready, CPU-safe
today. Genuinely the conservative choice and it would have worked. Rejected because the
GPU removes the constraint that made fastembed's catalogue the limit, and Qwen3 is the
stronger model.

**`Qwen3-Embedding-4B` (2560d).** Better retrieval, fits the 5070. Rejected on
constraint 2: GPU-only in practice, so the AskAI gate would need either a second model
(incomparable space) or a redesign. Not worth it for an increment.

**A different CPU model of the same dimension for the gate.** What "same dimensional CPU
embedder" could be read to mean. Rejected outright — dimension parity is not space
parity, and the failure is silent.

**Drop the embedding half of AskAI's gate** and rely on its `OFF_TOPIC` sentinel alone.
Would have freed the model size entirely. Not chosen; the gate keeps both mechanisms.

## Revisit when

- The backend actually deploys. That is when the ONNX CPU path gets built and its
  quantization drift measured against the gate threshold.
- The eval harness produces retrieval numbers. If 0.6B underperforms, the trade against
  4B can be re-argued with data rather than by reasoning about constraints.
- `spoin_db_2` is regenerated. That closes the temporary two-space divergence, and if it
  does not, this ADR is being violated.

adrs.title: ADR-0094: Generation and every heavy workload run locally; production hosts only the app backend
adrs.summary: Where each half of the system actually runs, and why the expensive half never touches the server.
adrs.content:
# ADR-0094: Generation and every heavy workload run locally; the production server hosts only the app backend

- **Status:** Accepted
- **Date:** 2026-09-05
- **Deciders:** project owner
- **Formalises:** the deployment split that [ADR-0092](/work/spoin#adr-0092)
  and task 0038's Phase 2 already assume without anything deciding it

## Context

This split has been operating since early September 2026 and shaping real
decisions, but it was only ever written down as *context* inside an ADR about an
embedding model. ADR-0092 opens with "the generation pipeline moves to the owner's
machine... only the app-serving backend deploys online" and reasons from it; the
`frog` compose service exists because of it; the deferred ONNX CPU path is deferred
because of it. Three consequences, no decision.

That is the shape CLAUDE.md warns about: a rule stated only in passing is a rule
the next session re-derives or quietly violates. The specific violation this
invites is cheap and permanent — adding a dependency to `apps/api` because
generation needs it, and discovering later that the deployed image carries several
gigabytes it never executes.

The two workloads have genuinely opposite profiles:

| | Generation / ingestion | Serving |
|---|---|---|
| Shape | bursty, batch, manual | constant, per-request |
| Bound by | GPU and provider quota | latency |
| Latency budget | minutes to days | ~50ms for a feed swipe |
| Frequency | when the owner runs it | every user interaction |
| Needs | torch, CUDA, LLM clients, the corpus | Postgres, FastAPI |

Sizing one machine to satisfy both means paying continuously for GPU-class
capacity in order to serve a feed that needs almost none of it. And the hardware
for the first column is already owned and otherwise idle: an RTX 5070.

## Decision

**There are exactly two environments.**

**Local machine (RTX 5070) + the GitHub remote.** Card generation and the whole
LLM pipeline, bulk embedding, corpus ingestion into `the_spoin_universe`, the eval
harness, benchmarks and probes. Run **manually** — there is no cron refill and no
plan to automate one for v1. Beta users are told a topic request is generated
manually and can take up to two days.

**The production server.** Only what the app needs to serve a request: the feed
read path, engagement, auth, AskAI. **As lightweight as possible.** If the
deployed backend does not execute it on a request path, it does not belong in the
deployed image.

### The operational rule this creates

**Before adding a dependency to `apps/api`, ask whether the production server
needs it.** If only generation or ingestion does, it belongs in a separate image.

This is already precedent rather than aspiration: the `frog` compose service
carries torch and the CUDA runtime — roughly 3GB — in its own image built from
`apps/frog/Dockerfile`, specifically so it stays out of the image that `api`,
`worker`, `seed` and `test` all build from. Folding it in would have put 3GB into
four images to serve one command.

### Why this constrains the embedder, permanently

The split is not clean, and the place it leaks is the reason ADR-0092 chose the
model it did. **Something still embeds on the live request path:** AskAI's
off-topic gate ([ADR-0077](/work/spoin#adr-0077))
embeds the user's question every turn and compares it against `topic.embedding`.
That cannot be queued or moved to the home PC.

So the embedding model must run on a CPU in the deployed backend, which is why
`Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B` was chosen over the stronger 4B that fits the 5070 just
fine. 0.6B is the largest size that keeps **one** model on both devices, and one
model is not negotiable: two models emitting the same number of dimensions do not
share a vector space, so a gate comparing a query vector from one against a topic
vector from the other compares noise, and nothing raises.

**Any future model choice inherits this constraint.** A model that cannot run on
a CPU is a decision to break the gate or to split the vector space.

## Consequences

**Easier.** The production server is small, cheap and boring, which is what a
serving tier should be. Generation gets a GPU for free and is not competing with
user traffic for anything. A full corpus re-embed is a minutes-long local
operation rather than a cloud cost, which makes embedding-model changes cheap to
evaluate instead of dreaded.

**Harder.** Generation does not happen unless someone runs it, and "up to two
days" is a real product promise made to beta users rather than a technical
detail. Two environments must be kept in step by hand — the `frog` image and the
`api` image install from the same `apps/frog/pyproject.toml` but with different
extras, and nothing enforces that they agree. The CPU/ONNX embedding path is owed
and unbuilt.

**Committed to.** Manual generation for v1. One embedding model that must run on
a CPU, indefinitely. A deployed image that deliberately cannot generate anything.

## Alternatives considered

**One environment that does both.** Simplest to reason about and to deploy.
Rejected on cost and shape: a GPU-class instance running continuously to serve a
read path that needs ~50ms of Postgres, when the GPU is already owned and idle at
home. It also couples generation load to user-facing latency, which the read/write
split in `docs/architecture/overview.md` exists to prevent.

**Generation in the cloud, on rented GPU or a provider API.** What the project did
before, and the [gemini-saga](../gemini-saga/README.md) is four weeks of what it
cost. Not rejected forever — this ADR is about v1 economics, and a provider that
behaves would change the arithmetic. Rejected for now because the local GPU makes
it free.

**Automate generation on a cron from the home PC.** Keeps the split, removes the
manual step. Rejected as premature: the pipeline is being actively rewritten
(task 0038's hybrid generator), and automating a thing that is changing weekly
means debugging the automation instead of the pipeline. Revisit when Phase 7 has
run end-to-end.

**Deploy the full image and simply never call the generation endpoints.** No
second image, no extras to keep in step. Rejected: an unused 3GB of torch is still
3GB in every pull, every restart and every image scan, and "we just don't call it"
is not a boundary — it is a habit.

## Revisit when

- **The backend actually deploys.** That is when the ONNX CPU path gets built and
  its int8 quantization drift measured against the gate's real threshold.
- **Generation stops being manual.** A cron or a queue on the home PC is a real
  change to the promise made to users, and to what "local" means operationally.
- **A second person needs to run generation.** "The owner's machine" stops being a
  location and becomes a role, and the corpus/model caches need somewhere shared.
- **AskAI's embedding gate is removed or redesigned.** It is the only thing forcing
  a CPU-capable embedder; without it the model size reopens.

adrs.title: ADR-0095: Cards carry real photographs from an open-licensed catalog, assigned server-side by retrieval
adrs.summary: Image assignment as a retrieval problem rather than a generation one.
adrs.content:
# ADR-0095: Cards carry real photographs from an open-licensed image catalog, assigned server-side by retrieval

- **Status:** Accepted
- **Date:** 2026-09-05
- **Deciders:** project owner, implementing session
- **Amends:** [ADR-0088](/work/spoin#adr-0088) — reverses its deliberate dropping of
  `author`/`licence`; attribution is now a stored, required field for images
- **Builds on:** [ADR-0089](/work/spoin#adr-0089) (retrieval),
  [ADR-0091](/work/spoin#adr-0091) (corpus hierarchy),
  [ADR-0066](/work/spoin#adr-0066) (a bad visual rejects its card)
- **Implemented by:** [task 0040](../tasks/0040-open-licensed-image-catalog.md)

## Context

The visual layer of a card is currently ASCII art and mermaid diagrams. ASCII is
deliberately **gags only** ([ADR-0079](/work/spoin#adr-0079)) — a hook, not
an explanation — and mermaid handles real diagrams
([ADR-0067](/work/spoin#adr-0067)). Neither can show what a thing
*looks like*. For a topic about Saturn, the Osirian cycle, or a nudibranch at 2,000
metres, a photograph is not decoration: it is the most information-dense thing that could
occupy that space, and we currently cannot put one there.

The corpus-authoring track already performs deep, sourced web research for every subject
(`docs/the_spoin_universe/procedure.md`, Phase C). It encounters the relevant imagery
during that research and throws it away. That is the asymmetry this ADR closes: the
expensive part — a human-supervised agent deciding which image genuinely illustrates a
subject — is already happening.

Three constraints shape the answer.

**We serve real users commercially.** The owner confirmed on 2026-09-05 that Spoin is a
commercial product. That removes any reliance on fair use or on non-commercial licences,
and it makes the naive version of this idea — re-hosting whatever the researcher found —
straightforward copyright infringement rather than a grey area.

**A bad visual now costs a whole card.** [ADR-0066](/work/spoin#adr-0066)
replaced the old "drop the visual, keep the card" degradation: art that cannot be made
valid rejects its card for regeneration. So any mechanism where the model can *get the
image wrong* now destroys an LLM call's output rather than degrading quietly.

**Not every subject can be illustrated.** Under an open-licence-only policy, internet
culture is essentially unavailable — memes carry stacked rightsholders (the underlying
photograph, the meme-maker's edits, the caption) and commercial use is precisely the case
fair use does not cover. Living people, current products and recent news photography are
similarly closed. A design that assumes every topic yields images will loop forever on the
ones that do not.

## Decision

**Antigravity delivers an open-licensed image catalog as part of the corpus. The images
are re-hosted on Cloudinary, ingested like documents, and assigned to cards server-side by
retrieval — never chosen by the model.**

### Only these licences, and the exclusions are not stylistic

Allowed: **CC0, public domain, CC BY, CC BY-SA**, plus the Unsplash, Pexels and Pixabay
licences.

**NonCommercial (NC) is excluded** because Spoin is commercial. This costs real material —
Schmidt Ocean Institute's deep-sea imagery among it — and is not negotiable while that
remains true.

**NoDerivatives (ND) is excluded because of the architecture, not the policy.** Cloudinary
is a transformation pipeline; cropping and resizing produce a derivative work. An ND image
would be disqualified the moment it was served at card width. This one is easy to miss
precisely because ND otherwise looks like the harmless restriction.

### Attribution becomes a stored, required field — reversing ADR-0088

CC BY and CC BY-SA require displayed attribution. ADR-0088 deliberately dropped `author`
and `licence` from `document`, and said in the same breath: *"If you find yourself needing
to record either, that is a real signal — raise it rather than smuggling it into
`source`."* This is that signal, taken at face value rather than worked around.

So the image catalog stores `licence`, `attribution` and `source_url` as NOT NULL, and the
card renderer gains a place to display attribution. An image that cannot state its licence
does not enter the catalog — which makes the constraint structural rather than a promise
the authoring track has to keep.

### The model never sees the images

Image assignment is **retrieval, not generation**: after a card is drafted, its text is
embedded and matched against image descriptions in `the_spoin_universe`, filtered to
images not already used in that topic, and the best match is attached.

The alternative — listing available images in the prompt and letting the model pick, then
removing used ones from the list — was considered seriously and rejected on three grounds.

**It is the approach this project already rejected once.**
[ADR-0021](/work/spoin#adr-0021) capped scene reuse by *counting server-side at
insert time*, explicitly "not trusted to the prompt", because "the model generates in
batches of ~10 and cannot see the rest of the corpus". Image assignment has exactly that
shape, and nothing about images makes the batching problem easier.

**It costs prompt budget the corpus work just finished protecting.** A menu of 450 images
at an id plus a short description is roughly 5.4k tokens on every generation call, before
any retrieved context. ADR-0089's table puts `ministral-8b` below the target throughput
above ~18k tokens, and task 0038's Phase 2 spent real effort keeping chunks small for that
reason. Server-side assignment costs zero prompt tokens.

**Under ADR-0066 its failure mode is now expensive.** A hallucinated or duplicated image
id would reject the card and burn the call. Server-side, the model emits no image
reference at all, so that failure class does not exist rather than being handled.

This is CLAUDE.md's rule applied literally: *the generator is trusted for taste, never for
constraints.* "No repeats within a topic" is a constraint.

### Availability is a planning input, so absence never loops

**The planner may only assign image cards up to the number of unused images the topic
actually has.** This is the load-bearing consequence of ADR-0066 and is the reason the
naive design is dangerous: if a card is planned as an image card, no licensable image
exists, and the missing visual rejects the card, the pipeline regenerates, plans another
image card, and fails again — an unbounded loop burning quota on a topic that can never
satisfy it.

The same shape already exists one line away in `generation/pipeline/state.py`: a `code`
card is never planned for a non-technical topic, because "the planner is trusted for
taste, not constraints". Image availability joins that check.

Consequently **"no image available" and "image is broken" are different outcomes**: the
first is a planning constraint that prevents the card being planned, the second is an
ADR-0066 rejection. Conflating them is what creates the loop.

### The coverage target is a ceiling, not a quota

The ambition is that a majority of cards carry a photograph. That figure is **read from
what the corpus can source, never aimed at.** Astronomy — NASA and ESA are wholly public
domain — may exceed it comfortably. Internet culture will sit near zero. Forcing a uniform
rate would push irrelevant images onto cards, which is worse than the ASCII gag it
replaced.

### One visual per card, and its kind is stored

**A card never carries both a photograph and an ASCII gag** (owner, 2026-09-05). There is
one visual slot, so `card.visual_id` is reused rather than images getting a column of
their own.

That makes the *kind* of visual something the card must state, and it cannot be inferred
from what already exists: `card_type` is a planning-time concept that is **never persisted
on the card**, and `archetype` is derived from `body`, which never contains the visual. So
a `visual_kind` enum accompanies `visual_id` — a real enum for ADR-0088's `document.kind`
reason, and not a guess from the id's string shape, which would make rendering depend on
an implicit format rule.

An image `visual_id` is a **cross-database reference by value**: the catalog is in
`the_spoin_universe`, so it cannot be a foreign key. Same boundary crossing ADR-0088
accepted for `chunk.topic_tags` and ADR-0089 for chunk-ID provenance, and it carries the
same obligation — nothing at the database level prevents a dangling reference, so the
renderer must survive one.

### Retraction: the image goes, and its cards are rebuilt without one

**An image that turns out not to be legally usable is removed, and every card citing it is
regenerated as an ASCII or diagram card** (owner, 2026-09-05) — not reassigned to a
different photograph.

Forcing the replacement to a non-image kind is the conservative choice and is deliberate:
if an image was wrong, the cheapest correct move is to stop gambling on that topic's
imagery rather than draw again from the same pool that produced the problem. It also makes
retraction terminate — a rule that reassigns could re-retract indefinitely.

Mechanically this is the query [ADR-0089](/work/spoin#adr-0089) already
argued provenance must make answerable — *"which cards did this retracted chunk ground?"* —
in its image form, and it is answerable for the same reason: the reference is stored, so it
is queryable. It is also why the cross-database reference below must tolerate dangling:
between removing an image and regenerating its cards, those cards point at nothing.

### Where the catalog lives, and where usage lives

**The catalog lives in `the_spoin_universe`**, delivered by Antigravity as an `images/`
manifest and ingested by the machinery task 0038's Phase 2 already built — parse, validate
against a contract, hash for idempotency, embed the description as a passage.

**Usage lives in `spoin_db_2`, on the card.** The corpus database is *derived and
rebuildable* (ADR-0088); image-to-card assignments are not. If a `used` flag lived in the
corpus, rebuilding it would silently orphan every assignment. Instead the card references
the image, and "unused" is a query — no active card in this topic references it — which
survives a corpus rebuild by construction.

### The manifest holds metadata, not binaries

Antigravity commits front-mattered manifest entries — source URL, licence, attribution,
description, tags — and **not the image files**. Hundreds of images per topic as git blobs
would bloat the repository permanently and irreversibly, and the corpus is deliberately
text-only.

The ingester fetches each image, uploads it to Cloudinary, and stores the returned URL.
Cloudinary is then our durable copy, which also removes link rot at the original source
from the failure set — a corpus meant to last cannot depend on a museum keeping a URL
stable.

## Consequences

**Easier.** The most information-dense visual a card can carry becomes available for the
subjects that warrant it. The expensive judgment — does this image actually illustrate
this idea — is made by a supervised researcher during work that already happens, not by a
model at generation time. Because assignment is retrieval, it costs no prompt budget and
no additional LLM call, on a path whose entire history is a fight for calls per minute.

**Harder.** A third visual kind joins ASCII and mermaid, and the renderer must handle all
three plus an attribution line. The corpus gains a delivery type with a genuinely
different contract. Cloudinary becomes a new external dependency with its own quota and
its own failure modes, and a second place where corpus state lives. Licence compliance is
now an ongoing obligation rather than a one-time check: an image whose licence is later
found to be misstated has to be removable, and the cards citing it repaired.

**Committed to.** Open licences only, indefinitely, and the coverage gaps that implies —
internet culture, living people, current products. Attribution displayed on cards. One
more thing that must be true about a corpus delivery before it can be ingested.

## Alternatives considered

**Re-host whatever the research turns up.** The original proposal, and by far the
cheapest. Rejected: copying third-party images to our own CDN and serving them
commercially is reproduction plus distribution, and the corpus contract already forbids
exactly this for text — *"Do not copy material you do not have the right to reproduce...
Cards will be shown to real users."* Images are worse, because unlike prose an image
cannot be restated in one's own words.

**Hotlink the originals instead of re-hosting.** Avoids storing a copy, and is at least
legally arguable where re-hosting is not. Rejected on reliability rather than law: link
rot, hosts that block hotlinking, no control over the served bytes, and a card whose
visual silently disappears months later. Cloudinary makes the image ours to serve.

**Generate images with a model.** No licensing question, unlimited coverage, fills the
brainrot gap. Rejected for this ADR: the product's claim is mastery of *true things*, and
a generated image of a nudibranch is a plausible nudibranch. It also reintroduces a
per-card generation cost on the write path. Worth revisiting for purely decorative slots
where no truth claim is made.

**Let the model pick from an in-prompt menu.** Discussed at length above: rejected on
ADR-0021's precedent, on prompt budget, and on ADR-0066 making its failure mode expensive.

**Put the image catalog in `spoin_db_2`.** No cross-database concern, and usage state sits
beside the images. Rejected: the catalog is authored material derived from a corpus
delivery, which is exactly what ADR-0088 separated, and it would make every image
re-delivery a migration against production.

## Revisit when

- **A topic is generated whose imagery is important and wholly unlicensable.** That is the
  moment to re-argue model-generated images for decorative slots, with a real example
  rather than in the abstract.
- **Cloudinary's free tier is exceeded.** Bandwidth, not storage, will be the binding
  constraint, and it arrives with user growth rather than corpus growth.
- **An image's licence is found to be misstated.** The first real test of whether the
  catalog can retract an image and repair the cards citing it — the image equivalent of
  ADR-0089's dangling-chunk question.
- **Spoin stops being commercial**, which would reopen the entire NC tier.

adrs.title: ADR-0096: Spoin canon is pinned into the prompt per call type, never retrieved
adrs.summary: The rules the product itself guarantees are not something a similarity search gets to decide is relevant.
adrs.content:
# ADR-0096: Spoin canon is pinned into the prompt per call type, never retrieved

- **Status:** Accepted
- **Date:** 2026-09-05
- **Deciders:** project owner, implementing session

> Amends [ADR-0088](/work/spoin#adr-0088), which implied `spoin_canon` is
> retrieved by relevance like any other document. It is not. ADR-0088's `kind` enum is
> unchanged and is now load-bearing in a second way: it is the filter that keeps canon
> *out* of the retrieval budget.

## Context

`the_spoin_universe` holds two kinds of document (ADR-0088). `topic_source` is
subject matter, relevant to the handful of calls about that subject. `spoin_canon` —
what a card is, [dual titles](/work/spoin#adr-0022),
[archetypes](/work/spoin#adr-0017), the ASCII box rule
([0021](/work/spoin#adr-0021)), quiz-gated progression
([0009](/work/spoin#adr-0009)), CLAUDE.md's silliness-in-the-hook-layer rule
— is small, and relevant to **nearly every generation call regardless of subject**,
because a small model does not know our conventions.

[ADR-0089](/work/spoin#adr-0089) then made retrieval share one packed
token budget across everything a prompt carries. That is where the two kinds stop
being able to share a mechanism.

## Decision

**Canon is pinned into the system prompt as a fixed preamble, chosen per call type at
design time. Retrieval asks for `topic_source` only, and the whole retrieval budget
goes to subject matter.**

`generation/prompts/canon.py` holds ten preambles composed from shared fragments, and
`generation/grounding.py` passes `kinds=[TOPIC_SOURCE]` on every search.

### Why competing for a retrieval slot is wrong in both directions

A canon chunk that wins a slot displaces a fact the card needed. A canon chunk that
loses one leaves a call that needed the box rule without it. Neither failure
announces itself: the first looks like a thin corpus, the second like a model that
ignores instructions. Pinning removes both by removing the contest.

### Pinned per call type, not wholesale

The five canon documents are ~21k characters, roughly 5,300 prompt tokens, and
ADR-0089's table puts `ministral-8b` under target throughput above ~18k. Most of it is
irrelevant to any one call — the box rule means nothing to a prose card, curriculum
decomposition means nothing to a card writer. So relevance is still decided; it is
decided **at design time by a static map** rather than per call by an embedding. That
is still "pinned" in the sense that matters: canon never competes for a slot and never
fails to appear.

### Condensed, and guarded against drift

The preambles are condensed rather than quoted: the corpus states each rule with the
reasoning that earned it, which is what a human reading the corpus needs and about
three times what a model following the rule needs. A rule's *why* is kept only where
the why is what makes the rule followable.

That makes the preambles a **derived artifact of a corpus another track revises**, so
`CANON_SOURCE_HASHES` records the sha256 of each source document and
`test_canon_preambles.py` recomputes them. Revising a canon document fails that test by
name. The guard raises rather than passing when it cannot find the corpus — the `api`
image carries no `docs/`, so the `test` service mounts it read-only.

## Consequences

**Easier.** Every call gets the conventions it needs, deterministically. The retrieval
budget buys only facts. The 40-column box rule had five independent phrasings across
the prompts and now has one, so it can be corrected in one place.

**Harder.** A new call type needs someone to decide which fragments it gets, and
getting that wrong is silent — a call that edits existing artwork without the box rule
produces art that renders broken, and nothing raises. (This was gotten wrong twice
while writing the map: `fetch_ascii_scenes` adapts a library scene and `correct_cards`
rewrites art, and neither was given the box rule at first.) Prompt size grew: every
call is +200 to +836 tokens before a single retrieved passage.

**Committed to.** Keeping the condensation current with a corpus we do not own, with a
test as the tripwire rather than a convention.

## Alternatives considered

**Retrieve canon like anything else (ADR-0088 as written).** No new mechanism, and
canon stays in one place. Rejected on the displaces-or-misses argument above: it is a
correctness question, and similarity search answers it probabilistically.

**Pin all five documents on every call.** Simplest possible pinning, and no static map
to get wrong. Rejected on cost: ~5,300 tokens on every call, most of it irrelevant to
that call, against a budget where prompt size decides whether the target rate is
reachable at all (ADR-0089's table).

**Quote the canon documents verbatim into the preambles.** No drift possible, because
the preamble *is* the corpus text. Rejected on the same token argument, and on a second
one: corpus prose is written to persuade a human that a rule is right, and a model does
not need to be persuaded.

**Generate the preambles at build time from the corpus.** No hand-maintained
condensation and no drift guard needed. Rejected: condensation is an editorial
judgement about which reasoning changes behaviour, and a build step that made it
automatically would either quote everything or drop the wrong halves.

## Revisit when

- A call type is added and the map has to grow. That is the moment to check whether a
  static map is still the right shape, and specifically whether anything that EDITS
  artwork is missing the box rule.
- The drift guard fails often enough to be noise rather than signal — that means the
  canon documents are still being authored, and pinning is running ahead of them.
- Phase 4 measures real prompt sizes. If pinned canon is a large share of a prompt that
  is over budget, the per-call-type map gets finer rather than the pinning being undone.

adrs.title: ADR-0097: One embedder, one vector space
adrs.summary: The embedder variable never reached the containers, so every stored vector was hash noise. The database was dropped and rebuilt rather than backfilled.
adrs.content:
# ADR-0097: One embedder, one vector space

- **Status:** Accepted
- **Date:** 2026-09-05
- **Deciders:** project owner

## Context

There were two embedders and two vector spaces.

`get_embedder()` returned a 384-dimensional model for `card.content_embedding`,
`topic.embedding` and `question.embedding`. `get_corpus_embedder()` returned
`Qwen/Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B` at 1024 dimensions for `the_spoin_universe`'s chunks
([ADR-0092](/work/spoin#adr-0092)). The split was not an oversight — the two
columns genuinely held incomparable vectors, and one factory would have made every
retrieval a dimension error rather than a silent quality loss. Task 0039 was where
they were meant to converge.

Two things forced the question earlier than planned.

**Nothing was using a real embedder on the spoin side at all.**
[Task 0039](../tasks/0039-embedder-never-reached-the-containers.md) found that
`docker-compose.yml` never passed `SPOIN_EMBEDDER` into the `api`, `worker` or `seed`
services, and compose injects only the variables a file names. `.env` set `fastembed`;
`Settings.embedder` fell back to its `hash` default. Every vector in `spoin_db_2` —
5,491 cards, 1,665 questions, 11 topics — was `HashEmbedder` output, which its own
docstring calls semantically meaningless. Nothing raised, because nothing could: a
hash vector has the right dimension and the wrong meaning, and every consumer
degraded quietly to lexical-overlap behaviour.

**The corpus is written for one model.** `the_spoin_universe` is authored and chunked
deliberately, and ingested with Qwen3. A second model over the same material buys a
second set of thresholds, a second calibration, and a standing invitation to compare
across the two.

So the choice was not "which of two models" but "why two at all".

## Decision

**One embedder serves everything: `Qwen/Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B` at 1024 dimensions.**
Cards, topics, questions, ASCII scene matching, AskAI's off-topic gate and corpus
retrieval all use it.

Concretely:

- `get_corpus_embedder()` is deleted. `get_embedder()` is the factory, and its
  dimension is `frog.universe.models.EMBEDDING_DIM` rather than a setting — that
  constant is what the columns were created with, so a configurable that disagreed
  could only ever produce vectors the database refuses. `Settings.embedding_dim` and
  `Settings.corpus_embedder`/`corpus_embedding_model` are gone.
- `card.content_embedding`, `question.embedding` and `topic.embedding` widen from
  `vector(384)` to `vector(1024)` (migration `feded8588fd8`). Postgres cannot cast
  between them, so the migration nulls each column first. The discarded vectors were
  hash noise, and `spoin_db_2` was dropped and rebuilt from the migration chain with
  the owner's explicit approval rather than backfilled.
- Every embedded row carries an **`embedding_model` stamp**, fed by a new
  `Embedder.model_name` property. This is task 0039's durable half: without it a
  column can hold two incomparable kinds of vector and no query, log line or test can
  tell. The stamp is enforced by the database, not by the nine call sites that write a
  vector — `CHECK ((embedding IS NULL) = (embedding_model IS NULL))` on all three
  tables (`b9876ddc6238`), because nine correct call sites are discipline and a tenth
  is one merge away.
- `apps/api/Dockerfile` takes an `EMBEDDER_BACKEND` build arg — `gpu` (cu128 torch)
  for the worker, `cpu` for the api and the test suite, `none` for `seed` and
  `universe-seed`, which run alembic and never embed. `Qwen3Embedder` already passes
  `device=None`, so sentence-transformers picks CUDA where it exists and CPU where it
  does not; only the wheel differs, never the code path.
- `docker-compose.yml` passes `SPOIN_EMBEDDER` and `SPOIN_EMBEDDING_MODEL` explicitly
  to every service that embeds — the missing line that caused task 0039.
- The test suite runs the real model on CPU rather than a stand-in. Task 0039 is what
  happens when the thing under test is not the thing that runs.

`HashEmbedder` stays, dimension-correct and meaningless, for one purpose: a stack that
boots with no model weights on disk. It is not a fallback to select in anger.

## Consequences

**Easier.** One vector space, one dimension, one set of thresholds to calibrate. A
retrieval query is embedded by the model its chunks were, structurally rather than by
convention. Task 0039's "flag and backfill must land together" problem disappears —
there is no second kind of vector to land beside.

**Harder, and paid for deliberately.** The deployed api image now carries torch, on an
image [ADR-0094](/work/spoin#adr-0094) argues should stay
minimal. **Measured, not estimated: 539MB -> 2.46GB.** The CPU wheel is far heavier than
the ~800MB its download size suggests, and the worker's cu128 image is 12.3GB. That is the cost of AskAI's off-topic gate embedding on
the request path ([ADR-0077](/work/spoin#adr-0077)) with
the same model as everything else, and it is why ADR-0092 chose 0.6B over the stronger
4B. `make test` also loads a real model, so the suite is slower than it was and CI
needs the weights cached; the `frog-model-cache` volume is mounted for exactly that.

**Unvalidated, and newly visible.** Every threshold in the system was calibrated
against hash vectors — `card_duplicate_threshold`, the accent-hue distances, and
retrieval's still-unset `min_score`. They are not stale, they are unmeasured. Real
vectors make measuring them possible for the first time; nothing here does that
measurement, and [task 0042](../tasks/0042-recalibrate-thresholds-against-real-vectors.md)
is where it lives.

**ADR-0094 is bent, not broken.** Heavy work still runs locally: only the worker gets
CUDA. What the production image gained is the ability to embed one short turn per
AskAI request on a CPU, which is what ADR-0092 sized the model for. ADR-0092's
deferred ONNX CPU path remains the way to drop torch from the deployed image; it is
now a size optimization rather than a prerequisite.

## Alternatives considered

**Keep two embedders, fix only the missing compose variable.** The one-line version of
task 0039. Rejected because it makes new vectors semantic while 5,491 stay hash, and a
column holding both is worse than a column holding either — comparisons across them
are noise and nothing raises. Fixing it properly meant a backfill anyway, and once a
backfill is on the table the dimension is free to change.

**Unify on the 384-dimensional model instead.** Cheaper: no migration, no torch in the
api image, no re-embed. Rejected because it points the wrong way — the corpus is the
asset, it is authored for Qwen3 and already ingested at 1024, and re-ingesting it to
match a weaker model chosen for its size would be optimizing the expensive thing for
the cheap one. BGE also needs a query prefix that this codebase never applied
(`FastEmbedEmbedder`'s docstring), so its recall was understated on top of everything
else.

**Package the ONNX CPU path now rather than torch.** `onnxruntime` is already in the
api image, so this would have kept it torch-free. Rejected as scope: it is a different
inference path from the one the corpus was embedded with, it needs its own export and
verification, and ADR-0092 deferred it until the backend actually deploys. Doing it
under time pressure to save 1.9GB on an image that is not yet deployed is the wrong
order. That number is the strongest argument for revisiting it once the backend ships.

**A build arg per service versus one image for all.** Installing torch unconditionally
is one line and no build matrix. Rejected because `api`, `worker`, `seed`, `test` and
`universe-seed` share the Dockerfile, and it would put ~3GB into the test and CI
images to serve one service — the exact argument `apps/frog/Dockerfile`'s header
makes. Measured after the fact, that argument was if anything understated: the CUDA
image is 12.3GB.

## Revisit when

- **The backend actually deploys.** Then torch's 1.9GB in the api image has a real
  bill attached, and ADR-0092's ONNX CPU path becomes worth building.
- **AskAI's gate latency is measured on a production-shaped CPU.** 0.6B was chosen to
  make this viable; if a turn's embedding is slow enough to be felt on the request
  path, the answer is the ONNX path or a smaller model on that path alone — and a
  second model on that path would reopen this ADR directly.
- **A thresholds pass runs against real vectors** (task 0042). If the numbers that
  come back say the model is wrong for topic canonicalization specifically, that is
  the evidence that would justify a second space — and it does not exist today.

## Related

- [ADR-0092](/work/spoin#adr-0092) — chose the model, and one model across two
  devices. This ADR extends that to one model across two *spaces*.
- [ADR-0087](/work/spoin#adr-0087) — says "shared 384-dim vector space";
  the sharing is now at 1024.
- [ADR-0094](/work/spoin#adr-0094) — the minimal production
  image, and what this costs it.
- [Task 0039](../tasks/0039-embedder-never-reached-the-containers.md) — the bug that
  forced the question, and where the stamp requirement comes from.
- [Task 0042](../tasks/0042-recalibrate-thresholds-against-real-vectors.md) — every
  threshold that is now measurable for the first time. (Task 0001, which task 0039
  pointed at, has been obsolete since ADR-0025 removed the thresholds it calibrates.)

adrs.title: ADR-0100: `the_spoin_universe` is a claim-qualified knowledge system, not a document collection
adrs.summary: What the corpus stores is claims with their qualifications attached, which is what makes a small model able to restate instead of recall.
adrs.content:
# ADR-0100: `the_spoin_universe` is a claim-qualified knowledge system, not a document collection

- **Status:** Accepted
- **Date:** 2026-09-05
- **Deciders:** project owner

## Context

Three delivered corpora — Rust, LangChain/LangGraph, and 10m air pistol — were read end to
end and assessed. The verdict: the authoring process produces **high-density expert survey
material**, strong on semantic density, mechanism-first explanation, cross-topic
relationships, and practical failure modes. Those properties are exactly what retrieval
wants and are not in question here.

What the corpus is **not yet** is a source of truth. A source of truth must be
authoritative, versioned, evidence-qualified, coverage-complete, internally coherent, and
pedagogically generative. The corpus is strong on the first property in spirit and weak on
the other five in mechanism.

**The dangerous failure is not omission.** It is that the prose sounds more certain than the
underlying evidence justifies, and nothing in the pipeline can tell the difference. frog
does not evaluate a passage's epistemic status — it retrieves it. The generator drafts from
it, the thinker gates against it, and Spoin teaches it. **A beautifully written falsehood
becomes a canonical falsehood**, and the gate cannot catch it, because the gate's own
grounding is that same passage.

Three concrete shapes of this, one per corpus:

- **False precision.** The 10m corpus prescribes 50/50 weight distribution, 30–40% grip
  pressure, 4–8 second firing windows, 60–80% of the cardiac R-R interval, exact trigger
  travel values, specific SCATT thresholds. Some are useful numbers. The prose presents them
  as universal physical law. *"If the shot has not broken by 8.0 seconds"* and *"many
  coaches use roughly 6–8 seconds as a practical upper bound because…"* are different kinds
  of statement, and the corpus collapses them.
- **Scientific-sounding mechanism that outruns its evidence.** The same corpus builds clean
  causal chains through baroreceptor discharge, cortical inhibition, alpha oscillations,
  sensory gating, photopigment bleaching. The problem is not that it sounds smart — it is
  that the reader gets no signal separating experimentally demonstrated fact from
  explanatory interpretation.
- **Temporal decay.** The LangChain corpus describes a moving ecosystem using *"modern"*,
  *"the standard"*, *"preferred mechanism"*, *"fully supported replacement"* — with
  `source_date: 2024` across material about current APIs. `Command` being preferred over
  conditional edges and *"a `TypedDict` declares a mapping of fields"* currently sit in the
  same epistemic bucket. One is version-scoped ecosystem guidance; the other is stable.

Rust wears the same problem in a different costume: *"Rust programs are designed as a DAG of
data transformations"* is a useful architectural heuristic stated as a description of the
language. Language guarantee, common implementation, Tokio behaviour, recommended practice,
and pedagogical mental model bleed together.

Two further gaps, both about what the corpus is *for*:

- **"Comprehensive-looking" is not comprehensive.** Nine dense Rust documents are not a
  zero-to-mastery curriculum; the LangChain corpus is an advanced survey that starts in the
  deep end. Density is being mistaken for coverage.
- **The unit is a fact, not a competency.** Documents are mostly `assertion → explanation`.
  Mastery needs `assertion → example → counterexample → misconception → boundary →
  consequence`, and for practical domains it needs learner variability — principle, common
  implementation, individual variation, diagnostic feedback, adaptation — rather than one
  optimal configuration.

## Decision

**`the_spoin_universe` is treated as a canonical knowledge system and one of the project's
primary assets, not a collection of essays.** Three commitments follow.

**1. Claims are first class, and epistemically qualified.** Every substantial claim belongs
to exactly one class, and the classes are never presented as equivalent:

| Class | Means | Example |
|---|---|---|
| `normative` | A specification, standard or rule says so | ISSF regulation, Rust reference, an RFC |
| `empirical` | Measured, with a population and conditions | "Elite shooters exhibited X under these conditions" |
| `mechanistic` | A causal explanation of why | The baroreceptor chain — the class needing most care |
| `heuristic` | Practical, usually works, not a law | "Prefer bounded channels" |
| `implementation` | True of one product/framework/version | "LangGraph 1.x prefers `Command`" |
| `pedagogical` | A teaching abstraction | "Rust as a DAG of data transformations" |

Forbidden conversions, stated as rules because each is a silent promotion: heuristic → law,
typical value → universal constant, implementation detail → conceptual truth, mental model →
formal specification, expert recommendation → experimentally proven fact.

**2. Versioning and provenance are part of truth.** Implementation-scoped claims carry
applicability (framework, version, `verified_on`) and status. Words like *modern*,
*standard*, *preferred*, *current*, *supported* may not appear without version or date
scope. The source hierarchy is explicit — primary specification → official documentation →
primary research → authoritative textbook → recognised expert material → secondary
synthesis → community heuristic — and **a lower tier is never silently promoted**. A
manufacturer's manual does not become an empirical law; a coach's recommendation does not
become a universal biological truth.

**3. Coverage is audited against competency, not page count.** Every topic gets an explicit
coverage matrix across twelve stages, from awareness and vocabulary through diagnosis,
trade-off reasoning, novel situations, cross-topic integration and expert judgment, marking
each stage strongly supported, weakly supported, or absent. *"We have nine documents"* stops
being an answer.

**The authoring workflow inverts.** Prose is authored **last**, after a domain map,
prerequisite graph, claim inventory, evidence mapping, competency map, misconception map,
application map, variability map, gap audit and version audit. It is executed by a family of
role-specific prompts rather than one generation prompt —
[`docs/handoff/corpus-authoring-system.md`](../handoff/corpus-authoring-system.md) is that
system.

**"Insufficient evidence" is a valid, expected deliverable.** The workflow must be able to
say the corpus is not good enough, and a gap must never be filled with plausible
model-generated material. This is the same rule the image contract states for imagery
([ADR-0095](/work/spoin#adr-0095), task 0040), for the same reason.

## Consequences

**Easier.** "Is this topic good enough to found mastery on?" becomes answerable from an
audit rather than from reading it and feeling impressed. Eventually a card can answer *why
does Spoin believe this* — concept, claim, evidence, scope, misconceptions addressed —
because provenance is retrievable rather than implicit.

**Harder.** Authoring gets substantially more expensive per topic, and the front half of it
produces no prose at all. The existing corpus does not meet this bar and will need a
retrofit pass. Epistemic labels are themselves authored, so they can be wrong — a
mislabelled claim is more dangerous than an unlabelled one, because it carries borrowed
authority.

**Committed to.** Density stays; this sits *above* the prose, and the corpus must not become
Wikipedia sludge. The existing retrieval contract is unchanged — document title/context on
every chunk, `##` sections as chunk boundaries, the token bound, human curation, and frog as
retrieval infrastructure rather than an authority.

## Alternatives considered
